words.ex: The mine produces halite for use in food preservation.
words.ex_cn: 这个矿场生产用于食品保存的岩盐。
words.en: Halite is a mineral form of sodium chloride, NaCl, commonly known as rock salt. It is commonly found in sedimentary evaporite deposits.

words.ex: He felt disgust when he saw the dirty food.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到脏兮兮的食物时，他感到厌恶。
words.en: A feeling of revulsion or profound disapproval aroused by something unpleasant or offensive.

words.ex: The company used a short slogan to attract customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司用了一个简短的口号来吸引顾客。
words.en: A short and striking or memorable phrase used in advertising or politics.

words.ex: Plants use chlorophyll to make food from sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 植物利用叶绿素利用阳光制造食物。
words.en: Chlorophyll is a green pigment found in plants and algae that is essential for photosynthesis, the process by which light energy is converted into chemical energy.

words.ex: The rules show uniformity in all schools.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则在所有学校中都保持一致。
words.en: The state or quality of being uniform; consistency.

words.ex: The child learns locomotion by crawling.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过爬行学习移动。
words.en: The ability to move from place to place.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.ex: The falconer expertly handled the majestic bird of prey.
words.ex_cn: 这位放鹰者熟练地操控着这只威严的猛禽。
words.en: A falconer is a person who keeps, trains, or hunts with falcons.

words.ex: The artistry of the painting amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的艺术性让每个人都惊叹。
words.en: The skill of an artist, or the quality of being artistic.

words.ex: The pterosaur flew high above the forest.
words.ex_cn: 翼龙在森林上方高高飞翔。
words.en: A pterosaur was a type of flying reptile that lived during the Mesozoic era.

words.ex: The daguerreotype was one of the earliest photographic processes.
words.ex_cn: 银版照相法是最早的摄影方法之一。
words.en: An early photographic process employing an iodine-sensitized silvered plate and mercury vapor.

words.ex: The child has malnutrition from not eating enough food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子因为吃不够饭而营养不良。
words.en: Malnutrition is a condition that results from eating a diet in which certain nutrients are lacking, in excess (too high in intake), or in the wrong proportions.

words.ex: Chemurgy aims to develop chemical processes that benefit agriculture.
words.ex_cn: 应用化学旨在开发有利于农业的化学工艺。
words.en: Chemurgy refers to the branch of applied chemistry that deals with the industrial application of organic raw materials, especially in the development of new products and materials.

words.ex: The merit of this plan is its simplicity.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划的优点是简单。
words.en: If something has merit, it has good or worthwhile qualities.

words.ex: He showed excellence in math competitions.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学竞赛中表现出色。
words.en: The quality of being outstanding or extremely good.

words.ex: He felt anxiety before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到忧虑。
words.en: Anxiety is a feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease about something with an uncertain outcome.

words.ex: The kitchen floor is made of linoleum.
words.ex_cn: 厨房的地板是用油毡做的。
words.en: Linoleum is a type of floor covering that is made from a mixture of linseed oil, cork dust, wood flour, and pigments pressed onto a canvas or jute backing.

words.ex: The tanker carried oil across the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这艘油轮将石油运过了大海。
words.en: A tanker is a ship, airplane, or truck designed to carry liquids, especially oil, in large quantities.

words.tr: n. 游牧民；流浪者；游牧生活；流浪生活
words.ex: The nomad walks with his sheep across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 游牧民带着他的羊群穿越沙漠。
words.en: A nomad is someone who has no permanent home and moves according to the seasons from place to place in search of food, water, and grazing land.

words.ex: The streetcar runs on tracks embedded in the street.
words.ex_cn: 有轨电车在嵌入街道的轨道上运行。
words.en: A streetcar is a vehicle that runs on rails along public streets and is used to carry passengers.

words.ex: The factory dumped sludge into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂把淤泥倾倒进河里。
words.en: Sludge is a thick, soft, wet mud or a similar viscous mixture of liquid and solid components, especially the product of an industrial or refining process.

words.ex: Children find amusement in playing games.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在玩游戏时感到快乐。
words.en: Amusement is the feeling that you have when you think that something is funny or entertaining.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A hooker is a term used to refer to a prostitute or, in rugby, a player who commits a foul by pulling an opponent.

words.ex: The astronaut walked on the moon.
words.ex_cn: 这名宇航员在月球上行走。
words.en: An astronaut is a person who is trained to travel in a spacecraft.

words.ex: The raindrops glistened on the windowpane.
words.ex_cn: 雨滴在窗玻璃上闪闪发光。
words.en: A raindrop is a single drop of rain.

words.tr: n. 通晓数国语言的人；语言学家；
words.ex: He is a linguist who speaks five languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位通晓五种语言的人。
words.en: A linguist is someone who studies language or languages, especially a person who studies linguistics.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: The circumference of the circle is 31.4 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的周长是31.4厘米。
words.en: The circumference of a circle is the distance around it.

words.ex: The dean gave a speech at the graduation ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 院长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。
words.en: A dean is a senior official in a college or university, who is in charge of a faculty or department or a group of students.

words.ex: The bacteria show high motility in warm water.
words.ex_cn: 这种细菌在温水中具有很高的运动能力。
words.en: The ability of an organism or fluid to move or be moved.

words.ex: He made his decision after long deliberation.
words.ex_cn: 他在深思熟虑后做出了决定。
words.en: Deliberation is the long and careful consideration of a subject.

words.ex: The forest shows regeneration after the fire.
words.ex_cn: 森林在火灾后显示出再生。
words.en: The process of renewal, restoration, and growth that makes cells, organisms, and ecosystems resilient to natural fluctuations or events that cause disturbance or damage.

words.ex: The knife left a nick on the wooden table.
words.ex_cn: 刀在木桌上留下了一道刻痕。
words.en: A nick is a small cut or notch in a surface or edge. As a verb, to nick means to make a small cut or notch in something, or to steal something.

words.ex: The pond is full of green alga.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里充满了绿色的藻类。
words.en: A simple, nonflowering, and typically aquatic plant of a large group that includes the seaweeds and many single-celled forms. Algae contain chlorophyll but lack true stems, roots, leaves, and vascular tissue.

words.ex: The papermaker's craft has been passed down through generations.
words.ex_cn: 造纸者的技艺已经代代相传。
words.en: A person or company that manufactures paper.

words.tr:
n. 炸弹
v. 投弹于；轰炸
words.ex: The bomb exploded at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹在中午爆炸了。
words.en: A bomb is a device which explodes and damages or destroys a large area.

words.ex: The honey has high viscosity.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜的黏度很高。
words.en: Viscosity is a measure of a fluid's resistance to flow. It describes the internal friction of a moving fluid.

words.ex: The soldiers walked across the battlefield.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们走过战场。
words.en: A battlefield is a place where a battle is fought.

words.tr:
n. 长柄大镰刀
v. 用长柄大镰刀割
words.ex: The farmer swings the scythe to cut grass.
words.ex_cn: 农夫挥动镰刀割草。
words.en: A scythe is a tool with a long curved blade at right angles to a long handle, used for cutting grass, grain, or other crops.

words.ex: He plays the flute every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上吹长笛。
words.en: A flute is a musical instrument of the woodwind family. You play it by blowing over a hole at one end while holding it sideways.

words.ex: The children walked carefully through the bog.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们小心地走过沼泽。
words.en: A bog is an area of wet muddy ground that is too soft to support a heavy body.

words.ex: The power plant generates several megawatts of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这座发电厂能生产数兆瓦的电力。
words.en: A unit of power equal to one million watts.

words.tr: n. 痴迷；困扰；着魔；强迫观念；
words.ex: His obsession with video games made him ignore his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的痴迷让他忽略了学业。
words.en: An obsession is an idea or thought that continually preoccupies or intrudes on a person's mind.

words.tr: phrase. 针头；小东西；没有头脑的人
words.ex: The pinhead of the needle is very small.
words.ex_cn: 针头非常小。
words.en: A pinhead is the small, flat end of a pin. Informally, it can also refer to a very stupid person.

words.tr:
n. 真空；空虚；
v. 用真空吸尘器打扫；
words.ex: The vacuum in space keeps no air.
words.ex_cn: 太空中的真空没有空气。
words.en: A vacuum is a space that contains no air or other gas, or a space from which most of the air or gas has been removed. It can also refer to a device that cleans floors and surfaces by sucking up dirt and dust.

words.ex: There is strife between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有争执。
words.en: Strife is angry or violent conflict between two people or groups.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: The statesman spoke wisely to calm the nation.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家明智地讲话以安抚国家。
words.en: A statesman is a respected political leader or figure, especially one who has had a long and successful career in politics.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: Homo erectus lived in Asia over a million years ago.
words.ex_cn: 直立人生活在一百多万年前的亚洲。
words.en: A misspelling or non-standard form of 'erect,' meaning to build or set up something upright.

words.ex: The currier treated the leather to make it softer.
words.ex_cn: 这位制革匠处理皮革使其变得更柔软。
words.en: A currier is a person whose job is to prepare and finish leather after it has been tanned.

words.ex: The shoemaking industry has seen a decline in recent years.
words.ex_cn: 制鞋业近年来有所衰退。
words.en: The activity or occupation of making shoes.

words.tr:
adj. 中途的；中间的
adv. 中途地；中间地
n. 娱乐场；游乐场
words.ex: He stopped midway to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他中途停下来休息。
words.en: Midway is used to describe something that is in the middle of a place or a period of time.

words.ex: Schoolchildren walk to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 学童每天早上走路去学校。
words.en: Schoolchildren are children who attend school.

words.ex: The neutron has no electric charge.
words.ex_cn: 中子不带电荷。
words.en: A neutron is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of every atom except that of simple hydrogen. It has no electric charge and a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.

words.tr:
adj. 种间的
n. 种间
words.ex: This research focuses on interspecies communication.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究专注于种间交流。
words.en: Existing or occurring between different species.

words.tr: n. 播种机；种植园主；花盆；种植园经营者
words.ex: The farmer used a planter to sow seeds in the field.
words.ex_cn: 农夫使用播种机在田里播种。
words.en: A planter is someone who plants crops or a machine used for planting seeds. It can also refer to a decorative container for plants.

words.ex: The playback of the concert was broadcasted on television.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会的重放录音在电视上播出。
words.en: The reproduction of previously recorded sounds or moving images.

words.ex: The recurrence of storms caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 风暴的反复出现造成了许多问题。
words.en: The return of a sign, symptom, or disease after a remission.

words.ex: He completed the registration for the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了这门课程的登记。
words.en: Registration is the act of officially recording something, especially in an official list or record.

words.ex: The old temple has four stone pillars.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙有四根石柱。
words.en: A pillar is a tall solid structure, which is usually used to support part of a building.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.ex: The knight wore heavy armor in the battle.
words.ex_cn: 骑士在战斗中穿着沉重的盔甲。
words.en: Armor is a protective covering that is used to prevent damage from being inflicted to an object, individual, or vehicle by direct contact weapons or projectiles, usually during combat.

words.tr: n. 追随者；拥护者；信徒；
words.ex: He is a loyal follower of the artist.
words.ex_cn: 他是这位艺术家的忠实追随者。
words.en: A follower is a person who supports and admires a particular person or set of ideas.

words.ex: The woodpecker taps on the tree every morning.
words.ex_cn: 啄木鸟每天早上在树上敲击。
words.en: A woodpecker is a bird with a strong beak that it uses to make holes in trees to find insects to eat.

words.ex: She picked a violet from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她从花园里摘了一朵紫罗兰。
words.en: A violet is a small plant that has purple or white flowers in the spring.

words.tr:
n. 前情；先行词；祖先（常复）
adj. 在 ... 之前的
words.ex: The word 'dog' is the antecedent of 'it' in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 在这句话中，'dog' 是 'it' 的先行词。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.tr:
pron. 无论哪个；
adj. 无论哪个的；
words.ex: You can pick whichever book you like.
words.ex_cn: 你可以选无论哪本书。
words.en: You use whichever to refer to any one of a group of things or people, when it does not matter which one is chosen or considered.

words.ex: The diamond is encased in glass.
words.ex_cn: 钻石被包裹在玻璃里。
words.en: To encase something means to cover or surround it completely in a case or close-fitting covering.

words.ex: The pendulum oscillate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆缓慢地摆动。
words.en: If an object oscillates, it moves repeatedly from one position to another and back again, or if a figure or value oscillates, it keeps moving up and down.

words.ex: The bustle of the market filled the morning air.
words.ex_cn: 市场的喧哗充满了早晨的空气。
words.en: If someone bustles somewhere, they move there in a hurried way, often because they are very busy or excited.

words.tr: v. 改编为戏剧；渲染；使戏剧化
words.ex: They dramatize the novel for the stage.
words.ex_cn: 他们将这部小说改编成舞台剧。
words.en: If a book or story is dramatized, it is written or presented as a play, film, or television drama.

words.tr: v. 滥伐…的森林；乱砍…的树木
words.ex: They deforest the land to build houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们砍伐森林来建造房屋。
words.en: To deforest means to remove the trees from an area of land.

words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.ex: The virus can infect people quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒能迅速感染人。
words.en: To infect someone or something means to cause them to have a disease or illness.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.ex: The movie recreates the battle of Waterloo.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影再现了滑铁卢战役。
words.en: To recreate something means to make it exist or happen again, or to make a copy of something that existed in the past.

words.ex: He will enroll in the English course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将注册英语课程。
words.en: To officially register or enlist oneself or someone else in a course, institution, or organization.

words.tr:
n. 瑕疵；污点；缺点
v. 玷污；损害
words.ex: The apple has a small blemish on its skin.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果的表皮上有一个小瑕疵。
words.en: A blemish is a small mark or flaw that spoils the appearance of something.

words.tr:
v. 蹲；蹲坐；擅自占住
n. 蹲；偷住的房子；蹲坐
adj. 矮而宽的；矮胖的
words.ex: He does a squat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做深蹲。
words.en: If you squat, you lower yourself towards the ground, balancing on your feet with your legs bent.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.tr: v. 对…表示极不赞成；强烈反对；轻视
words.ex: They deprecate old software.
words.ex_cn: 他们不推荐使用旧软件。
words.en: If you deprecate something, you criticize it or express your disapproval of it.

words.ex: The rebel fought against the king's rules.
words.ex_cn: 这位叛逆者反抗国王的法令。
words.en: A rebel is a person who opposes or fights against people in authority.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

words.tr: v. 散发；发射（光或热）；辐射
words.ex: The sun radiates heat and light.
words.ex_cn: 太阳散发出热量和光。
words.en: To send out rays or waves, especially of light or heat; to spread out from a central point.

words.ex: The teacher will stratify the students by age.
words.ex_cn: 老师会按年龄将学生分层。
words.en: To arrange or form into layers or strata.

words.tr: v. 将…分类；把…加以归类
words.ex: We categorize books by genre.
words.ex_cn: 我们按类型对书籍进行分类。
words.en: To categorize means to put people or things into groups according to their type or characteristics.

words.tr: v. 把…分类； 协调；相称；交际； 交往
words.ex: She assort the books by color.
words.ex_cn: 她把书按颜色分类。
words.en: To assort means to classify or arrange in groups according to kind, nature, or quality.

words.tr: v. 使分离；脱离；与…无关
words.ex: He tries to dissociate himself from the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让自己与坏消息脱离关系。
words.en: If you dissociate yourself from something or someone, you deliberately avoid being connected with them, especially because you want to avoid being affected by something bad or harmful.

words.ex: The teacher apportioned the books equally among the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师把书平均分给了学生们。
words.en: To apportion something is to divide it and share it out among several people or things.

words.ex: Fish abound in this river.
words.ex_cn: 这条河里鱼很多。
words.en: If things abound, or if a place abounds with things, there are very large numbers of them.

words.tr:
v. 织补
n. 织补
words.ex: She darned her socks with blue thread.
words.ex_cn: 她用蓝色线织补了她的袜子。
words.en: To darn means to repair a hole in a piece of clothing by sewing stitches across the hole.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.tr: v. 加浮雕花纹于；饰以浮饰；使凸出
words.ex: He embosses the card with his name.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字压印在卡片上。
words.en: To decorate a surface by making raised designs or patterns on it.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: He tried to seduce her with flowers and gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用鲜花和礼物引诱她。
words.en: To seduce someone means to persuade them to do something, especially something wrong or unwise, by making it seem attractive or exciting.

words.ex: The accident immobilized his leg.
words.ex_cn: 事故使他的腿无法动弹。
words.en: To prevent something or someone from moving or operating as normal.

words.ex: The magic show riveted the children's attention.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们的注意力。
words.en: A rivet is a short metal pin or bolt for holding together two plates of metal, its headless end being beaten out or pressed down when in place. As a verb, to rivet means to attract and hold the attention of someone completely.

words.tr: v. 由电视播送；用电视放映
words.ex: The news will televise the election results tonight.
words.ex_cn: 今晚电视将播出选举结果。
words.en: To broadcast something on television.

words.ex: He generalized the results from the small group to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他将小群体的结果概括为全体情况。
words.en: If you generalize, you say something that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: He conflates happiness with wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福和财富混为一谈。
words.en: To combine two or more things into one, especially in a way that is confusing or misleading.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.ex: He exclaim when he saw the surprise.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到惊喜时，他大喊起来。
words.en: If you exclaim, you say something suddenly and loudly, often because you are surprised, excited, or angry.

words.tr: v. 猛冲；猛投；猛烈碰撞
words.ex: The car hurtled down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 汽车飞速冲下山坡。
words.en: If someone or something hurtles somewhere, they move there very quickly, often in a uncontrolled way.

words.tr:
n. 不信任；名誉丧失；信誉丧失
v. 不信；败坏名声；使丢脸
words.ex: His lies brought discredit to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他的谎言使公司失去了信任。
words.en: To discredit someone or something means to cause them to lose people's respect or trust.

words.ex: The fence encircles the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏围绕着花园。
words.en: To encircle something or someone means to surround them completely.

words.tr: v. 使安静；安慰；使缓和
words.ex: She sang a song to soothe the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她唱了一首歌来安抚婴儿。
words.en: To soothe someone means to make them feel calmer and less anxious, upset, or angry.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.tr: v. 唤醒；唤起；使意识到
words.ex: The loud noise awakened him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音把他吵醒了。
words.en: If you awaken a feeling or emotion, or if it awakens, it starts to be felt or experienced.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: He computes the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快算出总成本。
words.en: If you compute a total, amount, or result, you calculate it.

words.tr: v. 加速；使更活跃；刺激
words.ex: The train will quicken as it leaves the station.
words.ex_cn: 火车离开车站时会加快速度。
words.en: To make or become faster or more active.

words.tr: v. 设防御工事；加强；增加营养物
words.ex: The soldiers fortify the hill with walls and trenches.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在山上用墙壁和战壕设防御工事。
words.en: To strengthen a place with defensive works so as to protect it against attack; to strengthen or invigorate someone mentally or physically.

words.ex: The dog gave a small nip to his leg.
words.ex_cn: 狗轻轻咬了他的腿一口。
words.en: To nip means to pinch, squeeze, or bite something quickly and sharply. It can also refer to taking a small amount of a drink.

words.ex: I presume he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假设他明天会到。
words.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

words.tr: v. 使变得低级；使变得低贱
words.ex: The fake materials cheapen the quality of the product.
words.ex_cn: 劣质材料降低了产品的品质。
words.en: To reduce the price of something; to make something seem less valuable or respected.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: The farmer shears sheep every spring.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每年春天给羊剪毛。
words.en: To shear means to cut the wool off a sheep or to cut or trim something with scissors or shears.

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.ex: He likes to moralize about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢就诚实问题说教。
words.en: To moralize means to express judgments about what is morally right and wrong, especially in a way that is considered to be annoying or unnecessary.

words.tr: v. 接种疫苗；预防接种
words.ex: The doctor will vaccinate the child tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 医生明天会给这个孩子接种疫苗。
words.en: To vaccinate someone is to give them a vaccine, usually by injection, to prevent them from getting a disease.

words.tr: v. 勉强维持；（靠节约）使更持久
words.ex: He had to eke out his income by taking on extra work.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不通过做额外的工作来勉强维持收入。
words.en: To eke means to make a living or support oneself with difficulty, often by adding to what one has in small amounts.

words.ex: He tried to loosen the tight screw.
words.ex_cn: 他试图拧松那颗紧的螺丝。
words.en: If you loosen something or if it loosens, it becomes less tight, less firmly fixed, or less strongly attached.

words.ex: The storm unleashed heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 风暴释放出大雨。
words.en: If you say that someone or something unleashes a powerful force, feeling, activity, or group, you mean that they suddenly start it or send it to move somewhere.

words.ex: He will unbind the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会解开这个包裹。
words.en: To unfasten or release something that is tied or bound.

words.tr:
v. 握紧；捏紧；咬牙切齿
n. 抓紧；咬紧；抓紧用具
words.ex: He clenched his fist when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时握紧了拳头。
words.en: To close or hold something very tightly, especially in a determined or angry way.

words.ex: They vie for the top prize.
words.ex_cn: 他们争夺最高奖项。
words.en: To compete eagerly with someone in order to do or achieve something.

words.ex: The two stories intertwine in the final chapter.
words.ex_cn: 这两个故事在最后一章交织在一起。
words.en: If two or more things are intertwined, they are closely connected with each other in many ways.

words.ex: He is chewing gum loudly.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大声地嚼口香糖。
words.en: To chew means to bite and grind food in your mouth so it becomes soft enough to swallow.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.ex: He endow a library with books.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一图书馆的书。
words.en: If someone is endowed with a particular quality or ability, they naturally have it.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: The blight destroyed the potato crops.
words.ex_cn: 这种枯萎病摧毁了马铃薯作物。
words.en: A blight is something that spoils or damages something, or a disease that affects plants.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.ex: The two rooms adjoin each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个房间彼此相邻。
words.en: If one room, place, or object adjoins another, they are next to each other.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr:
n. 滞后；延迟；
v. 落后；缓慢移动；
words.ex: There is a lag between the signal and the response.
words.ex_cn: 信号和响应之间有滞后。
words.en: If one thing or person lags behind another thing or person, their progress is slower than that of the other.

words.ex: The stone skimmed over the water.
words.ex_cn: 石头掠过水面。
words.en: To remove a substance from the surface of a liquid, or to read or consider something quickly in order to understand the main points, without studying it in detail.

words.ex: Add a dash of salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 给汤里加一点盐。
words.en: If you dash somewhere, you run or go there quickly and suddenly. A dash is a straight, horizontal line used in writing, for example to separate two main clauses whose meanings are closely connected.

words.tr: v. 迷惑；使迷惑不解；使糊涂
words.ex: The magic trick will mystify the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术会让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If you are mystified by something, you find it impossible to explain or understand.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.tr:
v. 豁免；
adj. 被免除的；
words.ex: The school exempted him from the test.
words.ex_cn: 学校免除了他的考试。
words.en: If someone or something is exempt from a particular rule, duty, or obligation, they do not have to follow it or do it.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.tr: v. （使）变直；（使）变平；（使）变整齐；
words.ex: He straightened the crooked picture on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把墙上歪斜的画扶直了。
words.en: To make something straight or to put something in order.

words.ex: He strives to finish his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力完成作业。
words.en: If you strive to do something or strive for something, you make a great effort to do it or get it.

words.ex: The kidneys excrete waste from the body.
words.ex_cn: 肾脏将废物排出体外。
words.en: If someone excretes waste matter from their body, they get rid of it in faeces, urine, or sweat.

words.tr:
n. 喷口；水管；水柱
v. 喷出；滔滔不绝地说
words.ex: The kettle has a small spout for pouring water.
words.ex_cn: 这个水壶有一个小喷口用来倒水。
words.en: If something spouts liquid or fire, or if liquid or fire spout out of something, it comes out very quickly with a lot of force.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.ex: A storm is about to impend.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴风雨即将来临。
words.en: If an event impends, usually an event that is unpleasant or unwanted, it is going to happen soon.

words.ex: They pave the road with stones.
words.ex_cn: 他们用石头铺路。
words.en: To cover a piece of ground with a hard, flat surface of pieces of stone, concrete, etc.

words.tr: v. 使通俗化；宣传；推广；使普及
words.ex: He wants to popularize science among children.
words.ex_cn: 他想在儿童中普及科学。
words.en: To make something known or liked by many people.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: The roof has a sharp slant.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶有一个陡峭的倾斜。
words.en: If something slants or if you slant it, it is at an angle rather than being straight up and down or straight from side to side.

words.tr:
n. 旁路；
v. 绕过；
words.ex: The city built a bypass around the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市建了一条绕过老城区的旁路。
words.en: If you bypass a place or a system, you avoid it or go around it instead of going through it.

words.tr: v. 晒太阳（取暖）；沉浸于
words.ex: He basks in the warm sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 他沐浴在温暖的阳光下。
words.en: If you bask in the sunshine, you lie somewhere sunny and enjoy the heat.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.ex: The char cleaned the office every morning.
words.ex_cn: 女清洁工每天早上打扫办公室。
words.en: To char is to burn something so that it becomes black or to work temporarily in a job.

words.tr: v. 使牵连其中；涉及；暗示；指明起因
words.ex: The evidence may implicate him in the crime.
words.ex_cn: 证据可能使他牵连进这起犯罪中。
words.en: To show or suggest that someone is involved in something illegal or morally wrong.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.tr: v. 施以催眠术；迷住；迷惑
words.ex: The dancer mesmerized the crowd with her slow movements.
words.ex_cn: 舞者用她缓慢的动作对观众施以催眠术。
words.en: If you are mesmerized by something, you are so interested in it or so attracted to it that you cannot think about anything else.

words.ex: The wind stiffened the cloth on the line.
words.ex_cn: 风把晾衣绳上的布吹硬了。
words.en: to make or become stiff or rigid; to make or become more severe or strict

words.ex: The vines entwine around the tree.
words.ex_cn: 藤蔓缠绕在树上。
words.en: To twist or twine together; interweave.

words.ex: The truck suffered an overload and broke down.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车因超载而抛锚了。
words.en: To load or burden someone or something excessively.

words.ex: The rain dampened the sound of the drums.
words.ex_cn: 雨减弱了鼓声。
words.en: To dampen something means to make it slightly wet, or to make it less strong or intense.

words.ex: The rain necessitated staying indoors.
words.ex_cn: 下雨使待在室内成为必需。
words.en: To necessitate something means to make it necessary for something to be done or to happen.

words.ex: The magnet can magnetize the iron nail.
words.ex_cn: 磁铁可以让铁钉磁化。
words.en: To magnetize something means to make it magnetic or to attract it strongly.

words.ex: The city plans to urbanize the village next year.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市计划明年将这个村庄城市化。
words.en: To make an area more urban by building houses, industries, and other facilities.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.tr: v. 使矿物化；使含无机化合物
words.ex: The water can mineralize rocks over time.
words.ex_cn: 水随着时间的推移可以使岩石矿化。
words.en: To convert into a mineral or to impregnate with minerals.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of jade.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条玉制的项链。
words.en: A hard, typically green stone used for ornaments and implements and consisting of the minerals jadeite or nephrite.

words.ex: The city plans to modernize its old subway system.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市计划现代化其老旧的地铁系统。
words.en: To modernize something means to change it so that it is more modern, for example by using more recent technology or methods.

words.ex: The city plan will revitalize the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市计划将使老城区复兴。
words.en: To revitalize something means to give it new life or energy.

words.ex: The loud noise stunned him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他震惊了。
words.en: To stun someone means to shock or surprise them very much.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.ex: The magic trick astounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们惊呆了。
words.en: If something astounds you, it surprises or shocks you very much.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: The factory will automate the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 工厂将自动化装配线。
words.en: To automate a factory, office, or industrial process means to put in machines which can do the work instead of people.

words.ex: The dogs outnumber the cats in this neighborhood.
words.ex_cn: 这个社区里的狗比猫多。
words.en: If one group of people or things outnumbers another, the first group has more people or things in it than the second group.

words.ex: We need to shorten the meeting to one hour.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要把会议缩短到一小时。
words.en: To make something shorter in length, duration, or extent.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: The two clocks synchronize automatically.
words.ex_cn: 这两座钟自动同时发生。
words.en: If you synchronize two activities, processes, or movements, or if you synchronize one activity, process, or movement with another, you cause them to happen at the same time and speed as each other.

words.ex: The sun can dehydrate your skin quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳会很快使你的皮肤脱水。
words.en: To dehydrate something means to remove all the water from it, often in order to preserve it. If you dehydrate, you lose too much water from your body, usually because of illness or extreme heat.

words.ex: The storm disorganized the city's traffic.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴使城市的交通陷入混乱。
words.en: To disorganize something means to disrupt its system or order, making it function less effectively.

words.ex: The cow will calve next week.
words.ex_cn: 这头母牛下周会产犊。
words.en: When a cow calves, it gives birth to a calf. When a glacier calves, pieces of ice break off from it.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.ex: He envisions a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 他想象一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: To envision something is to imagine it as a future possibility; it is often used to describe the act of foreseeing or planning for the future.

words.tr:
v. 定罪；宣判有罪
n. 罪犯；囚犯
words.ex: The court convicted him of theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院判定他犯有盗窃罪。
words.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

words.ex: He whittled a small bird from wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用木头削出了一只小鸟。
words.en: To whittle means to cut or shape a piece of wood by repeatedly cutting small slices from it, or to reduce something in size, amount, or extent by a gradual series of steps.

words.ex: The cat began to scat when it saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫看到狗时开始四处乱跑。
words.en: To go away quickly; a style of jazz singing characterized by improvised vocal sounds.

words.ex: The artist elongated the figure to create a sense of grace.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家拉长了人物形象，以创造出一种优雅的感觉。
words.en: To elongate something means to make it longer, especially by stretching it.

words.ex: The farmer feeds the pigs to fatten them.
words.ex_cn: 农夫喂猪使它们长胖。
words.en: To make or become fat or fatter.

words.ex: Heat will liquefy the ice.
words.ex_cn: 加热会使冰融化。
words.en: To make or become liquid.

words.ex: They want to immigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他们想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To come to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.tr:
v. 举起；投掷；起伏；喘息；呕吐
n. 举；投；掷；起伏
words.ex: He heave the box onto the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把箱子举到了桌子上。
words.en: To lift or haul something heavy with great effort; to throw something forcefully; to rise and fall rhythmically or with effort.

words.ex: The fence is painted with creosote to keep it from rotting.
words.ex_cn: 这围栏涂了煤焦油以防止腐烂。
words.en: Creosote is a dark brown oil that is used as a wood preservative. It is obtained by distilling tar from wood or coal.

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.ex: The kidneys reabsorb water from urine.
words.ex_cn: 肾脏从尿液中重新吸收水分。
words.en: If something is reabsorbed, it is absorbed again, especially after it has been released or excreted.

words.ex: He nodded in a blink.
words.ex_cn: 他一眨眼就点了点头。
words.en: To shut and open the eyes quickly, typically involuntarily.

words.ex: The clown entertains the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: To entertain someone means to amuse or interest them, for example by telling them stories or jokes, or by playing music for them.

words.ex: His talent overshadowed his brother's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华使他兄弟的成就黯然失色。
words.en: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.

words.ex: Please verify your email address.
words.ex_cn: 请核实你的电子邮件地址。
words.en: To verify something means to check or prove that it is true, accurate, or justified.

words.ex: The data was tabulated for easier analysis.
words.ex_cn: 数据被制成表格以便于分析。
words.en: To tabulate something means to arrange figures, facts, or information in a table or list so that it can be easily understood or compared.

words.ex: He reset the password to log in again.
words.ex_cn: 他重置了密码以便再次登录。
words.en: To set again or differently; to adjust or fix in a new or different way.

words.ex: The company will retrain its workers for new machines.
words.ex_cn: 公司会再培训员工以适应新机器。
words.en: To teach someone new skills or to teach them again so that they can do a different job or do their old job in a different way.

words.tr: v. 重新调整；重新适应
words.ex: He had to readjust his schedule after the meeting was moved.
words.ex_cn: 会议改期后，他不得不重新调整自己的日程。
words.en: To adjust or adapt again, especially to a new situation or environment.

words.ex: The mayor will reelect next year.
words.ex_cn: 这位市长明年将再次当选。
words.en: To elect someone again to a particular position.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.ex: The stars destine her to be a leader.
words.ex_cn: 命运注定她将成为一位领导者。
words.en: To determine the future or the fate of something or someone in advance.

words.ex: She blesses her children every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上为孩子们祝福。
words.en: If someone is blessed with a particular good quality or skill, they have that good quality or skill.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；攫住
n. 紧抓；离合器；一窝雏；一小群；紧要关头
words.ex: He clutched the rope tightly when he slipped.
words.ex_cn: 当他滑倒时，他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To clutch something means to hold it tightly, usually because you are afraid or anxious. In a vehicle, the clutch is a pedal that you press with your foot to change gears.

words.ex: He helped to lade the boat with supplies.
words.ex_cn: 他帮忙把补给装上船。
words.en: To load or to put cargo onto a ship or vehicle.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.ex: They revere their grandfather for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 他们因祖父的智慧而尊敬他。
words.en: If you revere someone or something, you respect and admire them greatly.

words.ex: He is a stocky man with strong arms.
words.ex_cn: 他是个身材敦实、手臂强壮的人。
words.en: A stocky person is broad and solidly built.

words.tr: adj. 按时间先后顺序排列的
words.ex: The events are listed in chronological order.
words.ex_cn: 这些事件按时间顺序列出。
words.en: If things are described or shown in chronological order, they are described or shown in the order in which they happened.

words.ex: The hemispheric wind pattern affects the weather.
words.ex_cn: 半球风模式影响天气。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a hemisphere.

words.ex: The rocks were in a semimolten state due to the intense heat.
words.ex_cn: 由于高温，岩石处于半熔状态。
words.en: Partially melted; in a state between solid and liquid.

words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.ex: He works in a custodial facility for juveniles.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个少年监禁设施工作。
words.en: Custodial is used to describe something relating to the legal responsibility for taking care of someone, especially a child, or for looking after property.

words.tr: adj. 沉重的；笨重的；沉闷的
words.ex: He carried a ponderous box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他搬着一个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: Something that is ponderous is very heavy or is very slow and clumsy because of its weight or size.

words.ex: The old system is cumbersome and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧系统复杂而低效。
words.en: Something that is cumbersome is large and heavy and therefore difficult to carry, wear, or handle.

words.tr: adj. 笨重的；难处理的；臃肿的；庞大的
words.ex: The box was unwieldy and hard to carry.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子又大又笨重，很难搬。
words.en: An unwieldy object is difficult to move or handle because of its size, shape, or weight.

words.ex: The child drew a figural shape on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在纸上画了一个图形。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of figures or representations of figures, especially in art.

words.ex: The smell of flowers was pervasive in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花的香味遍布整个花园。
words.en: Something that is pervasive is present or noticeable throughout a place or thing.

words.ex: His knowledge of history is superficial.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史的了解是表面的。
words.en: If you describe someone as superficial, you disapprove of them because they do not think deeply, and have little understanding of anything serious or important.

words.ex: The postglacial landscape has many lakes.
words.ex_cn: 冰川消退后的地貌有许多湖泊。
words.en: Relating to or occurring during the period following the last glacial epoch.

words.tr: adj. 不可改变的；永恒不变的
words.ex: The password is immutable and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 密码是不可更改的。
words.en: If you say that something is immutable, you mean that it cannot be changed at all.

words.tr: adj. 永无变化的；始终如一的
words.ex: The speed of light is invariable.
words.ex_cn: 光速是不变的。
words.en: An invariable thing or quality never changes or is always the same.

words.ex: The punishment was disproportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚与罪行不成比例。
words.en: Something that is disproportionate is surprisingly large or small in comparison to something else.

words.tr: adj. 不纯的；不纯洁的；肮脏的；渎神的
words.ex: The water is impure and not safe to drink.
words.ex_cn: 这水不纯净，不能喝。
words.en: Something that is impure is not clean or is mixed with another substance, and is therefore often not suitable for use.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

words.tr: adj. 引起麻烦的；不方便的；
words.ex: The late bus is inconvenient for me.
words.ex_cn: 这趟晚班公交车让我很麻烦。
words.en: If something is inconvenient, it causes problems or difficulties for you.

words.ex: The rain was unavoidable during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨期间，下雨是不可避免的。
words.en: If something is unavoidable, it cannot be avoided or prevented.

words.ex: The damage to the environment is irreversible.
words.ex_cn: 对环境的破坏是不可逆转的。
words.en: If a change is irreversible, it cannot be changed back to how it was before.

words.ex: It is disadvantageous to skip breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 不吃早餐是不利的。
words.en: If something is disadvantageous to you, it is likely to cause you difficulties or problems.

words.ex: The kiwi is a flightless bird.
words.ex_cn: 几维鸟是一种不会飞的鸟。
words.en: Flightless birds are birds that through evolution lost the ability to fly.

words.ex: His behavior is unacceptable.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为是不可接受的。
words.en: If you describe something as unacceptable, you strongly disapprove of it or object to it and feel that it should not be allowed to continue.

words.tr: adj. 无法解决的；不能溶解的
words.ex: The problem is insoluble with the current tools.
words.ex_cn: 用当前的工具无法解决这个问题。
words.en: If a problem or mystery is insoluble, it is impossible to solve or explain.

words.tr: adj. 不加辨别的；不加批判的
words.ex: He accepted the news uncritical.
words.ex_cn: 他毫不质疑地接受了这个消息。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncritical, you mean that they do not judge whether someone or something is good or bad, right or wrong, before supporting or believing them.

words.ex: The words on the sign are indistinct.
words.ex_cn: 标志上的字模糊不清。
words.en: not clear or sharply defined

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不明确的
words.ex: The result is indeterminate.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不确定的。
words.en: If something is indeterminate, you cannot say exactly what it is.

words.tr: adj. 不受限制的；无限制的；完整清晰的
words.ex: The kids have unrestricted access to the playground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们可以自由进入游乐场。
words.en: If something is unrestricted, it is not limited or controlled by anyone or anything.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不相关的；
words.ex: His opinion is irrelevant to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见与这个决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as irrelevant, you mean that it is not important to or not connected with the present situation or discussion.

words.tr: adj. 不合适的；不相称的；不协调的；
words.ex: His funny hat was incongruous with the formal suit.
words.ex_cn: 他的滑稽帽子与正式西装不搭配。
words.en: Something that is incongruous is strange when considered together with other aspects of a situation.

words.ex: The movie's world feels unreal.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的世界感觉不真实。
words.en: If you describe something as unreal, you mean that it is so strange, unusual, or extreme that it seems like something from a dream or a story rather than something real.

words.tr: adj. 草本植物的；叶状的
words.ex: The garden was filled with herbaceous plants.
words.ex_cn: 花园里种满了草本植物。
words.en: Herbaceous plants are plants that have non-woody stems. Their above-ground growth largely or totally dies back in winter in the temperate zone, but they may have underground plant parts (roots, bulbs, etc.) that survive.

words.ex: The doctor checked his intestinal health.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠道健康。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the intestines.

words.tr: adj. 高潮线与低潮线之间的
words.ex: Crabs live in the intertidal zone.
words.ex_cn: 螃蟹生活在潮间带。
words.en: The intertidal zone is the area of the shore that is covered by water at high tide and exposed at low tide.

words.ex: The report gives an exhaustive list of all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告给出了所有规则的详尽列表。
words.en: If you describe a study, search, or list as exhaustive, you mean that it is very thorough and complete.

words.ex: He used an idiomatic expression in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中使用了一个惯用表达。
words.en: If you refer to someone's idiomatic use of a language, you mean that they use it in a way that sounds natural and correct to native speakers of that language.

words.ex: He visited his natal village for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 他第一次回到了自己的出生村庄。
words.en: Relating to the place or time of one's birth

words.ex: He read a biographical book about Einstein.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于爱因斯坦的传记书籍。
words.en: Relating to the events of a person's life as written by someone else.

words.tr:
adj. 竖直的；直立的；
adv. 笔直地；
words.ex: The picture is hanging upright on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画垂直地挂在墙上。
words.en: If you are sitting or standing upright, you are sitting or standing with your back straight, rather than bending or lying down.

words.tr: adj. 表示允诺的；约定支付的
words.ex: He signed a promissory note to pay back the loan.
words.ex_cn: 他签署了一张本票来偿还贷款。
words.en: Relating to or containing a promise.

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.ex: The old paper looks yellowish.
words.ex_cn: 这张旧纸看起来发黄。
words.en: Somewhat yellow in color.

words.ex: The subterranean tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接着两栋大楼。
words.en: Existing, occurring, or done under the earth's surface.

words.tr: adj. 地志的；地形学上的
words.ex: The map shows topographic details of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图展示了山脉的地形细节。
words.en: Relating to the arrangement of the physical features of an area.

words.ex: The team studied geoarchaeological layers near the ancient site.
words.ex_cn: 团队研究了古遗址附近的地质考古层。
words.en: Relating to the study of the geological aspects of archaeological sites and materials.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

words.ex: The cactus is prickly and hurts if you touch it.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌是多刺的，碰了会疼。
words.en: Something that is prickly feels as if it has a lot of small sharp points on it, or is covered with them. It can also describe someone who is easily annoyed or offended.

words.tr: adj. 如骨的；多骨的；瘦骨嶙峋的
words.ex: He has a bony hand that looks thin and weak.
words.ex_cn: 他有一只骨瘦如柴的手，看起来又细又弱。
words.en: If you describe someone as bony, you mean that they are very thin so that their bones stick out.

words.ex: The children played with multicolored balloons.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们玩着五颜六色的气球。
words.en: Having many colors.

words.ex: The gravelly road made the car bounce badly.
words.ex_cn: 这条多碎石的路让车子颠簸得很厉害。
words.en: A gravelly area of land is covered with gravel. A gravelly voice is low and rough.

words.tr: adj. 多用途的；多功能的
words.ex: This tool is multipurpose and can be used for many tasks.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具是多功能的，可以用于许多任务。
words.en: Having or serving several purposes.

words.tr: adj. 多汁的；利润丰厚的；有趣味的
words.ex: The apple is juicy and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果多汁又甜。
words.en: If you describe something as juicy, you mean that it is very interesting or exciting, especially because it involves scandalous or personal information.

words.ex: He gave a vicious smile before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前露出一个恶毒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vicious, you mean that they are violent and cruel, or that they are intended to cause someone great harm or suffering.

words.ex: The children are noisemaking during recess.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在课间休息时制造噪音。
words.en: The act or process of making noise.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: adj. 繁重的；累赘的；难于负担的
words.ex: The homework was burdensome and took all night.
words.ex_cn: 作业负担沉重，花了一整晚时间。
words.en: If you describe something as burdensome, you mean it is very difficult to cope with or manage because it is so heavy, large, or complex.

words.ex: The boy has an abnormal heartbeat.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的心跳不正常。
words.en: Deviating from what is normal or usual, typically in a way that is undesirable or worrying.

words.tr: adj. 累断腰的；非常辛劳的
words.ex: He did backbreaking work in the fields every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在田里干繁重的活。
words.en: If you describe a task as backbreaking, you mean that it is extremely hard physical work.

words.ex: The game was uncompetitive because one team was much stronger.
words.ex_cn: 这场比赛毫无竞争力，因为一支队伍强得多。
words.en: If you describe a business or its prices as uncompetitive, you mean that it is unable to compete successfully with other businesses because its prices are too high or the goods or services it offers are not of a sufficiently high quality.

words.ex: The sensor detects nonvisual signals like heat.
words.ex_cn: 传感器检测像热量这样的非视觉信号。
words.en: Not involving or relating to sight or vision.

words.tr: adj. 没有生产能力的；与生产无关系的
words.ex: He spent the day in nonproductive meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他一整天都泡在没有成效的会议里。
words.en: Not producing or capable of producing goods or services that have economic value.

words.tr: adj. 不能理解的；费解的
words.ex: The instructions were incomprehensible.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明让人完全看不懂。
words.en: If something is incomprehensible, you cannot understand it because it is so complex or unusual.

words.tr: adj. 分歧的；发散的；趋异的；
words.ex: The two friends had divergent opinions about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友对这部电影的看法不同。
words.en: If two things diverge, they are different from each other, or they become different from each other.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: The scenic lake attracted many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 风景优美的湖泊吸引了许多游客。
words.en: Relating to or resembling scenery; picturesque.

words.ex: The planktonic organisms float in the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 这些浮游生物在海洋中漂浮。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of plankton, the small and microscopic organisms drifting or floating in the sea or fresh water.

words.ex: The child gave an imaginative story about flying cats.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子讲了一个关于会飞的猫的富有想象力的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone or their ideas as imaginative, you are praising them because they are easily able to think of or create new or exciting things.

words.ex: The teacher explained the conceptual meaning of gravity.
words.ex_cn: 老师解释了重力的概念含义。
words.en: Relating to or based on mental concepts.

words.tr:
adj. 高尚的；
n. 贵族；
words.ex: He made a noble decision to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个高尚的决定去帮助穷人。
words.en: If you say that someone is a noble person, you admire and respect them because they are unselfish and morally good.

words.ex: The barnacle is commensal on the whale.
words.ex_cn: 藤壶依附在鲸鱼身上共生。
words.en: A commensal is an organism that lives in a relationship with another organism where one benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed.

words.ex: He walked alone in the lone park.
words.ex_cn: 他独自走在空无一人的公园里。
words.en: If you talk about a lone person or thing, you mean that they are alone.

words.ex: He gave an intentional wrong answer to confuse the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他故意答错答案来迷惑老师。
words.en: Something that is intentional is done on purpose, not by chance.

words.ex: The sand is siliceous and very fine.
words.ex_cn: 这种沙子是硅质的，非常细腻。
words.en: Containing or resembling silica; of, relating to, or containing silica or a silicate.

words.tr: adj. 过度的；过高的；过分的；
words.ex: The restaurant charged an exorbitant price for a small salad.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅对一份小沙拉要了过高的价格。
words.en: If you describe something such as a price or fee as exorbitant, you are emphasizing that it is much higher than it should be.

words.ex: The garden has superabundant flowers in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天，这个花园里花朵非常多。
words.en: Exceeding what is necessary or normal; excessively abundant.

words.tr: v. 过分强调；“overemphasize”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He overemphasized the importance of grades.
words.ex_cn: 他过分强调了成绩的重要性。
words.en: If you say that something cannot be overemphasized, you are emphasizing that it is very important.

words.ex: This phone is out-of-date.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了。
words.en: No longer fashionable or current; old-fashioned.

words.ex: The soup was too watery and tasted bland.
words.ex_cn: 这汤太稀了，味道淡。
words.en: Something that is watery contains, resembles, or consists of water.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 适于航海的；远洋航行的
words.ex: He works on a seagoing ship.
words.ex_cn: 他在一艘远洋船上工作。
words.en: Suitable for or engaged in sea voyages.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
words.en: If someone is hospitable, they are friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers.

words.tr:
adj. 激进的；好战的
n. 激进；好战
words.ex: He is a militant who protests every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天抗议的激进分子。
words.en: A militant person is someone who is engaged in warfare or combat, or who is aggressively active in a cause.

words.ex: The team worked in a harmonious way.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队以和谐的方式合作。
words.en: A harmonious situation, relationship, or agreement is one in which people are friendly and helpful to one another, and in which there is no serious disagreement or argument.

words.ex: The riparian plants grow near the river.
words.ex_cn: 河岸植物生长在河边。
words.en: Relating to or situated on the banks of a river.

words.ex: Hormonal changes can affect mood.
words.ex_cn: 激素变化会影响情绪。
words.en: Relating to or caused by hormones.

words.ex: DNA is a type of nucleic acid.
words.ex_cn: DNA是一种核酸。
words.en: Relating to or constituting the nucleus of a cell or the nuclei of atoms.

words.tr: adj. 完全的；荒凉的；光秃秃的；僵硬的；严厉的
words.ex: There was a stark difference between the two results.
words.ex_cn: 这两个结果之间有完全的差异。
words.en: Stark means complete, severe, or obvious in a way that is impossible to avoid noticing.

words.ex: It's preposterous to think cats can drive cars.
words.ex_cn: 认为猫会开车是极其荒谬的。
words.en: If you describe something as preposterous, you mean that it is extremely unreasonable and foolish.

words.ex: It's ridiculous to think he can run a mile in one minute.
words.ex_cn: 认为他能在一分钟内跑完一英里是荒谬的。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is ridiculous, you mean that they are very foolish.

words.ex: The field is unplanted this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这块地没有播种。
words.en: Not planted with seeds or crops.

words.ex: The teacher gave timely help when I was stuck.
words.ex_cn: 当我遇到困难时，老师及时提供了帮助。
words.en: done or occurring at a favorable or useful time; opportune.

words.ex: The food at this restaurant is superb.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅的食物极佳。
words.en: If something is superb, its quality is very good indeed.

words.ex: The micro worm is hard to see with naked eyes.
words.ex_cn: 这个微小的蠕虫用肉眼很难看到。
words.en: Extremely small in scale or scope.

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.tr:
adj. 急动的；颠簸的；抽筋的
n. 肉干
words.ex: His jerky movements made the camera footage blurry.
words.ex_cn: 他急动的动作让视频画面变得模糊。
words.en: If you describe something as jerky, you mean that it moves in a way that is not smooth, but rather with sudden stops and starts.

words.ex: The pattern is geometrical and simple.
words.ex_cn: 这个图案是几何形状的，而且很简单。
words.en: Relating to geometry, or according to its methods and principles.

words.ex: He gave a succinct answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简洁的回答。
words.en: Something that is succinct expresses facts or ideas clearly and in few words.

words.ex: The water is alkaline and tastes bitter.
words.ex_cn: 这种水是碱性的，尝起来苦。
words.en: Having a pH greater than 7; relating to or containing an alkali.

words.tr: adj. 语言交际能力的（尤指用外语）；乐意沟通的；
words.ex: He is very communicative in English, even when he makes mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他用英语交流时很有能力，即使犯了错误。
words.en: Someone who is communicative talks to people, for example about their feelings, and tells people things.

words.ex: The old tree has a stout trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有一个粗壮的树干。
words.en: Someone who is stout is rather fat or heavy.

words.ex: The app has an interactive game for kids.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用有一个适合孩子的交互式游戏。
words.en: An interactive computer program or system is designed to involve the user in the exchange of information.

words.tr: adj. 教育学的；教学法的
words.ex: The teacher used pedagogic methods to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师使用了教学法来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Pedagogic relates to the methods and theory of teaching.

words.ex: The plants grow in successional order.
words.ex_cn: 这些植物按 succession 的顺序生长。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by succession; following in order or sequence.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.ex: The doctor studied the anatomical structure of the heart.
words.ex_cn: 医生研究了心脏的解剖结构。
words.en: Relating to the structure of the bodies of people and animals.

words.ex: The price of the phone is prohibitive for most students.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机的价格对大多数学生来说太贵了。
words.en: If the cost of something is prohibitive, it is so high that it prevents people from buying it or doing it.

words.tr: adj. 强健的；强壮的；结实的；
words.ex: The dog is robust and runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很强健，每天跑步。
words.en: Strong and healthy; vigorous. (of an object) sturdy in construction.

words.ex: The old law was antiquated by the new government.
words.ex_cn: 旧法律被新政府废除了。
words.en: To make something old-fashioned or obsolete.

words.tr: adj. 某群体的；截面的；可组合的；区域的
words.ex: The sofa is sectional and fits the corner well.
words.ex_cn: 这张沙发是模块化的，非常适合角落。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of sections or parts; partial or local in nature.

words.tr: adj. 不顾一切的；极度渴望的；绝望的；
words.ex: He made a desperate attempt to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾一切地试图救那个孩子。
words.en: If you are desperate, you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to try anything to change it.

words.tr:
adj. 健壮的；硬朗的
v. 强拉硬拖
words.ex: He is still hale at age 80.
words.ex_cn: 他80岁了依然身体健康。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially an old person, as hale, you mean that they are healthy.

words.ex: The country has a militaristic government.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个军国主义的政府。
words.en: If you describe a country or its policies as militaristic, you are critical of them because they believe that it is necessary to have strong armed forces and to use them aggressively in order to gain power or to achieve their aims.

words.ex: The metal cracked along intergranular paths.
words.ex_cn: 金属沿着晶间路径开裂。
words.en: Relating to or situated between the grains or crystals of a substance, especially a metal.

words.ex: The difference is discernible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个差异肉眼可见。
words.en: able to be discerned; perceptible

words.ex: The apartment is rentable for $800 a month.
words.ex_cn: 这套公寓每月租金为800美元。
words.en: If something is rentable, it can be rented or is profitable to rent.

words.ex: The change in her mood was observable.
words.ex_cn: 她情绪的变化是能察觉到的。
words.en: Something that is observable can be seen or noticed.

words.ex: These two words are interchangeable in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 这两个词在这个句子中可以互换使用。
words.en: If one thing is interchangeable with another, the first can be used instead of the second because it has the same function or meaning.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: The weather was dire, with heavy rain and strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常可怕，下着大雨，刮着大风。
words.en: If you describe a situation as dire, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or serious.

words.tr: adj. 可渗透的；可渗入的；
words.ex: The soil is permeable, so water passes through easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种土壤是可渗透的，所以水很容易通过。
words.en: If a substance is permeable, it allows liquids or gases to pass through it.

words.tr: adj. 可花费的；可消耗的；可牺牲的
words.ex: He is an expendable worker in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他是公司里可有可无的员工。
words.en: If someone or something is expendable, people can get rid of them or allow them to be destroyed when they are no longer needed.

words.tr: adj. 可出售的；适于销售的；
words.ex: This painting is marketable because many people like it.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是可以出售的，因为很多人喜欢它。
words.en: If something is marketable, it is easy to sell because people want to buy it.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.tr: adj. 可以计量的；可量化的
words.ex: The results are quantifiable and clear.
words.ex_cn: 这些结果是可以量化的，而且清晰。
words.en: If something is quantifiable, it can be measured or expressed in numbers.

words.tr: adj. 可诱导的；可导致的
words.ex: The gene is inducible by light.
words.ex_cn: 这个基因可以被光诱导。
words.en: Capable of being induced or caused by a specific stimulus or condition.

words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.ex: He joins extracurricular activities after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后参加课外活动。
words.en: Extracurricular activities are those that fall outside the realm of the normal curriculum of school or university education, performed by students. Extracurricular activities exist at all levels of education, from 4th-6th, junior high/high school, college and university education.

words.tr: adj. 飞行的；空运的；空中传播的；
words.ex: The airborne soldiers jumped from the plane.
words.ex_cn: 这些空降士兵从飞机上跳下。
words.en: In the air; flying or transported by air.

words.tr: adj. 炎热的；炽热的；情欲强烈的
words.ex: The torrid sun burned the dry land.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的太阳炙烤着干涸的土地。
words.en: If you describe something as torrid, you mean that it is very hot and dry.

words.ex: The new house has a spacious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所新房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A spacious room, building, or place is large in size or area, so that you can move around freely in it.

words.ex: The wall has a cracklike line after the earthquake.
words.ex_cn: 地震后，墙上出现了一条裂缝般的线条。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a crack.

words.tr: adj. 不受个人感情影响的；没有人情味的；
words.ex: The judge gave an impersonal decision based on the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官基于法律作出了不受个人感情影响的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as impersonal, you mean that they do not show any emotion about the person they are dealing with.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.tr:
adj. 两足动物的
n. 两足动物
words.ex: The robot walks in a bipedal way.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人以双足的方式行走。
words.en: Relating to or using two feet or legs for walking.

words.tr: adj. 相接的；相邻的；接壤的
words.ex: The two countries are contiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家是相邻的。
words.en: Being in contact; touching or next to each other.

words.tr: adj. 权宜的；临时凑合的；
words.ex: He used a makeshift table made of boxes and a board.
words.ex_cn: 他用箱子和木板做了一个权宜的桌子。
words.en: A makeshift object or arrangement is one that is made or done quickly and without much skill, using whatever is available at the time.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: If you say that something is breathtaking, you mean that it is extremely beautiful or amazing.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；不计后果的；
words.ex: He drove reckless and got into an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他开车鲁莽，结果出了事故。
words.en: If you say that someone is reckless, you mean that they act in a way which shows that they do not care about danger or the effect their behaviour will have on other people.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌烦的；令人烦恼的；
words.ex: The loud noise is bothersome.
words.ex_cn: 这嘈杂的声音令人厌烦。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as bothersome, you mean that they cause bother or difficulties.

words.ex: The cat has a fluffy tail.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫有一条蓬松的尾巴。
words.en: Something that is fluffy is soft and light, with many small, loose pieces or parts.

words.ex: The uneaten food was thrown away.
words.ex_cn: 没吃的食物被扔掉了。
words.en: Not eaten; remaining after others have eaten.

words.tr: adj. 不盈利的；无利可图的；没有用的
words.ex: The small shop is unprofitable because few customers come.
words.ex_cn: 这家小店不赚钱，因为顾客很少。
words.en: If an activity or business is unprofitable, it does not make a profit.

words.tr: adv. 详细地；极微地；极小心精确地
words.ex: He explained the plan minutely.
words.ex_cn: 他详细地解释了这个计划。
words.en: In a detailed or precise manner; every minute.

words.ex: The old man gave an enigmatic smile.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人露出了一个神秘的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as enigmatic, you mean they are mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The chef made a deft cut with the knife.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用刀熟练地切了一下。
words.en: A deft action is skilful and often quick.

words.tr: adj. 模糊的；不确定的；无限期的
words.ex: He gave an indefinite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个不确定的答案。
words.en: If you describe something as indefinite, you mean that it has not been decided or defined clearly, or that it has no clear limit or end.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr:
adj. 牛的；似牛的；迟钝的
n. 牛；牛科动物
words.ex: The bovine grazed quietly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 那头牛在田野里安静地吃草。
words.en: Relating to or resembling cattle; slow or dull in manner.

words.ex: It was fortuitous that he found his keys just before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他在出发前刚好找到钥匙，真是幸运。
words.en: If you describe something as fortuitous, you mean that it happens by chance rather than by anyone's planning or intention.

words.ex: The study of embryological development is crucial in understanding the formation of organisms.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎发育的研究对于理解生物体的形成至关重要。
words.en: relating to the branch of biology and medicine concerned with the study of embryos and their development.

words.tr:
adj. 疲倦的；厌烦的
v. （使）厌倦；厌烦
words.ex: He looked weary after working all day.
words.ex_cn: 他工作了一整天后看起来很疲惫。
words.en: If you are weary, you are very tired.

words.tr:
adv. 漂流地；漫无目的地
adj. 漂泊的；漫无目的的；脱落的
words.ex: The boat was adrift in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 小船在海上漂流。
words.en: If something is adrift, it is floating on the water and not fastened to anything or controlled by anyone.

words.tr:
adj. 在水上漂浮；有偿债能力
adv. 在水上漂浮；有偿债能力
words.ex: The boat stayed afloat during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船在风暴中保持漂浮。
words.en: If someone or something is afloat, they are floating on water or in the air.

words.tr: adj. 无重大事件的；太平无事的
words.ex: The trip was uneventful.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行很平静，没什么事发生。
words.en: If you describe a period of time as uneventful, you mean that nothing interesting, exciting, or important happened during it.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr: adj. 破坏性的；引起混乱的；
words.ex: The new technology caused disruptive changes in the market.
words.ex_cn: 这项新技术给市场带来了破坏性的变化。
words.en: Causing or tending to cause disruption.

words.tr: adj. 应受严厉谴责的；可悲的；极糟糕的
words.ex: The living conditions in the slums were deplorable.
words.ex_cn: 贫民窟的生活条件非常糟糕。
words.en: If you say that something is deplorable, you think that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.ex: The pinniped seal basked on the rocky shore.
words.ex_cn: 这只鳍足类的海豹在岩石海岸上晒太阳。
words.en: A pinniped is a marine mammal belonging to the group Pinnipedia, which includes seals, sea lions, and walruses.

words.ex: The walls were painted a drab color.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁被刷成了土褐色。
words.en: If you describe something as drab, you think that it is dull and boring to look at or experience.

words.tr: adj. 天真无邪的；无辜的；
words.ex: The innocent child smiled at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个天真无邪的孩子对陌生人笑了。
words.en: If someone is innocent, they did not commit a crime which they have been accused of.

words.ex: He showed deep affectional love for his dog.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的狗表现出深厚的情感爱意。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by affection or emotional ties.

words.tr: adj. 表示庆祝的；庆祝性的
words.ex: They had a celebratory dinner after the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼后他们举行了一场庆祝晚餐。
words.en: Relating to or marking a celebration.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.ex: It was an utter mistake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个完全的错误。
words.en: To say something or to make a sound with your voice; complete or absolute.

words.tr: adj. 决定性的；权威性的；确定的；
words.ex: The test results were definitive.
words.ex_cn: 这些检测结果是决定性的。
words.en: A definitive book, performance, or report is considered to be the best of its kind that has ever been done or that will ever be done.

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.tr: adj. 人类学的；人类学上的；
words.ex: The anthropological study showed how ancient tribes lived.
words.ex_cn: 这项人类学研究展示了古代部落的生活方式。
words.en: Relating to the study of human societies and cultures and their development.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈善事业的；
words.ex: She gave charitable donations to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 她向穷人捐赠了仁慈的善款。
words.en: A charitable organization or activity helps and supports people who are ill, very poor, or who have disabilities.

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.ex: The cactus has fleshy stems to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有肉质的茎来储存水分。
words.en: If you describe something as fleshy, you mean that it is thick and soft, like flesh.

words.tr: adj. 僧侣的；教士的；圣职的；手写草书体的；神圣风格的
words.ex: The hieratic script was used primarily by priests.
words.ex_cn: 僧侣体文字主要由祭司使用。
words.en: Hieratic relates to priests or the priesthood, especially in ancient Egypt, or to a form of ancient Egyptian script that was used for religious texts.

words.ex: The king ate a sumptuous meal in his palace.
words.ex_cn: 国王在他的宫殿里享用了一顿丰盛的饭菜。
