words.en: A subtitle is a secondary or explanatory title, or a translation of the dialogue in a film or television program, displayed at the bottom of the screen.

words.ex: The discovery of Ambulocetus fossils provided crucial insights into the transition of whales from land to sea.
words.ex_cn: 陆行鲸化石的发现为鲸从陆地到海洋的过渡提供了关键的见解。
words.en: Ambulocetus is an extinct genus of early cetaceans that lived during the early Eocene epoch. It is known for its transitional features that illustrate the evolutionary transition from land-dwelling ancestors to modern whales.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.ex: The adequacy of the food supply was checked daily.
words.ex_cn: 食物供应的适当性每天都会被检查。
words.en: The state or quality of being adequate; sufficiency for a particular purpose.

words.ex: His resourcefulness helped him solve the problem with no tools.
words.ex_cn: 他的足智多谋帮助他在没有工具的情况下解决了问题。
words.en: Resourcefulness is the ability to deal skillfully and promptly with new situations, difficulties, or problems.

words.ex: The fallen tree was an obstruction on the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstruction is something that blocks a road, passage, or entrance, or the act of blocking something.

words.ex: The software has five different modules.
words.ex_cn: 这个软件有五个不同的模块。
words.en: A module is one of the separate parts of a course of study, especially at a college or university.

words.ex: My forebear came from Ireland long ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先很久以前来自爱尔兰。
words.en: Your forebears are your ancestors, especially your grandparents or earlier relatives.

words.ex: She wore a diamond ring on her finger.
words.ex_cn: 她手指上戴着一枚钻石戒指。
words.en: A diamond is a precious stone consisting of a clear and colorless crystalline form of pure carbon, the hardest naturally occurring substance.

words.ex: He is at the forefront of new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他处于新技术的前沿。
words.en: The forefront is the most forward part of something, especially in a literal or metaphorical sense, indicating the leading position in a particular field or activity.

words.tr: adv. 无论什么；任何(用于否定句中以加强语气)；
words.ex: You can eat whatever food whatsoever.
words.ex_cn: 你可以吃任何食物。
words.en: used to emphasize a negative statement

words.tr:
adj. 俯卧的；平卧的；给（悲伤等）压倒的
v. 使俯伏；使拜倒
words.ex: He fell prostrate on the ground after the race.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，他瘫倒在了地上。
words.en: If you prostrate yourself, you lie down flat on the ground, usually in front of someone, as a way of showing respect or submission. It can also mean to be extremely tired or emotionally drained.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.ex: He sows seeds in the garden every spring.
words.ex_cn: 他每年春天都在花园里播种。
words.en: To sow means to plant seeds in the ground so that they will grow into plants.

words.ex: He preaches kindness every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都宣扬仁爱。
words.en: If you preach, you give a talk on a religious or moral subject during a religious service.

words.tr: v. 重新刷新；翻新；整修
words.ex: They will refurbish the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新这栋老房子。
words.en: To refurbish something means to clean it, decorate it, and provide it with new equipment or facilities, especially so that it is more attractive or more useful.

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.ex: He will repay the loan next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月会偿还贷款。
words.en: If you repay a loan or a debt, you pay back the money that you owe to the person who you borrowed or took it from.

words.ex: He can describe the picture in one sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他能用一句话描述这幅画。
words.en: If you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened.

words.ex: The project cost overrun the budget.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的成本超过了预算。
words.en: If an army or a group of people overruns a place, they take control of it by force. If something such as a place or a piece of land is overrun by things or people, it is filled with them and they spread everywhere.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.ex: The teacher commends her for working hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师表扬她学习努力。
words.en: If you commend someone or something, you praise them formally.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: Our team won the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 我们的团队赢得了足球比赛。
words.en: A team is a group of people who play a particular sport or game together against other similar groups of people.

words.ex: The memory of the accident still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故的记忆仍然长期困扰着他。
words.en: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time. A place that is haunted is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.ex: He wore formal attire to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了正式服装去参加婚礼。
words.en: Clothes, especially fine or formal ones.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.ex: He smashed the glass with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把玻璃打碎了。
words.en: To break something into pieces violently and noisily, or to cause something to do this by dropping, throwing, or hitting it.

words.tr:
n. 弹跳；跳动；
v. 弹跳；反弹；
words.ex: The ball had a high bounce on the concrete.
words.ex_cn: 球在混凝土上弹跳得很高。
words.en: If something bounces or if you bounce it, it moves away from a surface after hitting it.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.tr:
v. 放逐到孤岛上
n. 孤立的人；褐红色；栗色
adj. 褐红色的；栗色的
words.ex: The ship was marooned on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船被困在了一个小岛上。
words.en: Maroon is used to describe a dark reddish-brown color. As a verb, it means to leave someone in a place from which they cannot escape, especially on a deserted island.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The apple will decompose in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 苹果会在土壤中分解。
words.en: If something decomposes, or if it is decomposed, it decays or breaks down into smaller parts or substances.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.tr:
adj. 有生命的；有活力的
v. 使具活力；做成动画
words.ex: The cartoon characters are animate and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 这些卡通角色是有生命的，充满活力。
words.en: To animate something means to give it life or to make it lively and energetic.

words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.ex: The farmer decided to replant the field with a different crop.
words.ex_cn: 农民决定用不同的作物改种这片田地。
words.en: To replant means to plant something again or in a new place.

words.tr: v. 重新组织；改组；整顿
words.ex: He will reorganize his desk tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会重新整理他的书桌。
words.en: To reorganize something means to change the way in which it is organized, arranged, or structured.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定付款必须按月进行。
words.en: If you stipulate a condition or stipulate that something must be done, you say clearly that it must be done.

words.tr: n. 过头的行为；过分的行为
words.ex: The presentation was a bit of overkill for such a small audience.
words.ex_cn: 对这么小的观众群来说，这个演讲有点过犹不及。
words.en: Overkill refers to an excess of what is required or suitable, especially in the context of using more force, resources, or effort than is necessary to achieve a goal.

words.tr:
n. 焊料；焊锡
v. 焊接；焊合
words.ex: He used solder to fix the broken wire.
words.ex_cn: 他用焊料修理了断掉的电线。
words.en: Solder is a fusible metal alloy used to create a permanent bond between metal workpieces.

words.tr: v. 后退；减弱；退出（某种活动）
words.ex: The flood waters begin to recede.
words.ex_cn: 洪水开始退去。
words.en: If something recedes, it becomes more distant or less noticeable.

words.ex: He exhale slowly after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后慢慢呼出气。
words.en: To exhale means to breathe out air from your lungs.

words.tr:
n. 遇难船只；残骸；
v. 破坏；毁坏；
words.ex: The wreck lies at the bottom of the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这艘遇难船只沉在海底。
words.en: If something such as a ship or a plane is wrecked, it is damaged so much that it cannot be repaired or it is completely destroyed.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.ex: He tries to memorize the words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天试着记住这些单词。
words.en: To memorize something means to learn it so well that you can remember it perfectly.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.ex: The teacher will inspect our homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会检查我们的作业。
words.en: If you inspect something, you look at it very carefully, usually in order to find out something about it.

words.ex: She sang softly to allay his fears.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声唱歌以缓解他的恐惧。
words.en: If you allay someone's fears or doubts, you stop them feeling afraid or doubtful.

words.ex: Subtract 5 from 10 to get 5.
words.ex_cn: 从10中减去5得到5。
words.en: If you subtract one number from another, you take the first number away from the second.

words.tr:
v. 溅；洒
n. 洒、溅等的声音
words.ex: Rain spattered the windows.
words.ex_cn: 雨点溅在窗户上。
words.en: To spatter means to scatter or splash (a liquid) in small drops over an area. It can also refer to the act of defaming or sullying someone's reputation.

words.ex: His converse was the opposite of what he said earlier.
words.ex_cn: 他的相反言论与他之前说的话相反。
words.en: To engage in conversation; to talk informally with someone.

words.ex: He tries to economize by walking to work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过步行上班来节省开支。
words.en: To economize means to use less money, time, or resources than usual in order to save them.

words.tr:
n. （统治者的）配偶；一组
v. 厮混；结交
words.ex: The king walked with his consort at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 国王在游行中与他的配偶一起行走。
words.en: A consort is a husband or wife, especially of a reigning monarch. As a verb, it means to habitually associate with someone, typically with the implication of a close or intimate relationship.

words.ex: He unraveled the knotted string.
words.ex_cn: 他把打结的绳子拆散了。
words.en: To unravel means to separate or disentangle the threads of a fabric or a rope, or to solve or explain something that is complicated or mysterious.

words.ex: My auntie gave me a cake for my birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我伯母送了我一块蛋糕作为生日礼物。
words.en: Someone's auntie is the sister of their mother or father, or the wife of their uncle.

words.ex: They exalt their hero with cheers.
words.ex_cn: 他们用欢呼赞美他们的英雄。
words.en: To exalt someone or something means to praise them very highly.

words.tr: v. 送医院治疗；使住院
words.ex: He was hospitalized after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后被送进了医院。
words.en: To admit someone into a hospital for treatment.

words.tr: v. 行为不端；行为无礼貌
words.ex: The boy misbehaved in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上行为不端。
words.en: If someone, especially a child, misbehaves, they behave in a way that is not acceptable to other people.

words.tr: v. 连根拔起；迁离；根除；
words.ex: The storm uprooted the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树连根拔起了。
words.en: If you uproot yourself or if you are uprooted, you leave a place where you have lived for a long time and go to live somewhere else.

words.ex: He inter his dog in the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的狗关在后院里。
words.en: To place a dead body in the ground or in a tomb.

words.ex: The ancient city was entombed beneath volcanic ash.
words.ex_cn: 这座古城被火山灰掩埋。
words.en: To place a dead body in a tomb or grave.

words.ex: The volcano erupts suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 火山突然喷发。
words.en: If a volcano erupts, it throws out smoke, fire, and melted rocks.

words.tr:
v. 喷出；涌出；呕吐
n. 呕吐物；喷出物
words.ex: The factory spews smoke into the air.
words.ex_cn: 工厂向空气中排放烟雾。
words.en: To spew means to expel something, especially liquid, gas, or small particles, in large quantities and with force. It can also refer to the act of vomiting.

words.tr:
n. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
v. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
words.ex: The car crash happened at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碰撞发生在十字路口。
words.en: If a vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: He halved the cake into two equal parts.
words.ex_cn: 他把蛋糕切成两等份。
words.en: To halve something means to divide it into two equal parts, or to reduce it by half.

words.tr:
n. 栖枝；鲈鱼；
v. 栖息；处于（高处）；
words.ex: The bird sat on a perch near the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟停在树旁的一根栖枝上。
words.en: A perch is a branch or rod where a bird rests or a high position where someone or something is located. As a verb, it means to rest or be located in a high position.

words.ex: He prays every morning before breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃早餐前祈祷。
words.en: To pray means to speak to God in order to give thanks or to ask for something.

words.ex: The teacher will enlighten the students about the truth.
words.ex_cn: 老师将向学生们阐明真相。
words.en: To enlighten someone means to give them more knowledge and greater understanding about something.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.ex: He used a hammer to knap the flint.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子敲击燧石。
words.en: To strike sharply; to break or shape (stone or flint) by striking it.

words.tr: v. 切断；脱离；切成两段
words.ex: He severed the rope with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀把绳子割断了。
words.en: To sever something means to cut through it or to break it off completely.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: The landlord will evict the tenant for not paying rent.
words.ex_cn: 房东会因为租客不付房租而将他驱逐。
words.en: To evict someone means to force them to leave a house or piece of land, usually because they have not paid the rent or have broken the law.

words.ex: He misinterprets her words as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的话，以为是生气。
words.en: To interpret wrongly; misunderstand.

words.ex: He insured his car against accidents.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的车投保了意外险。
words.en: If you insure yourself or your property, you pay money to an insurance company so that if you become ill or if your property is damaged or stolen, the company will pay you a sum of money.

words.tr:
v. 染上点颜色
n. 一丝痕迹；色调
words.ex: The sky has a tinge of pink at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空有一丝粉红色。
words.en: A tinge of a colour, feeling, or quality is a small amount of it.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.tr: v. 使石化；使僵化；吓呆
words.ex: The lightning petrified the tree into stone.
words.ex_cn: 闪电把树变成了石头。
words.en: To petrify means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.

words.tr: v. 使不满意；使不满足；使失望
words.ex: The slow service dissatisfy the customers.
words.ex_cn: 缓慢的服务使顾客不满意。
words.en: If something dissatisfies you, it does not satisfy you or give you pleasure.

words.ex: She moistened the dry bread with water.
words.ex_cn: 她用水把干面包弄湿了。
words.en: To make something slightly wet.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.ex: The police tried to subdue the angry man.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图制服那个愤怒的人。
words.en: To subdue someone or something means to bring them under control by using force or persuasion.

words.tr: v. 构思；使形成观念；使概念化
words.ex: He tries to conceptualize the problem before solving it.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决问题之前试图理解这个概念。
words.en: To conceptualize something means to form an idea or concept of it in your mind.

words.ex: The roller coaster exhilarates the children.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让孩子们感到兴奋。
words.en: To make someone feel very happy and excited.

words.tr: adj. 合法的；法律认可的；合理的；
words.ex: This contract is legitimate and signed by both parties.
words.ex_cn: 这份合同是合法的，并由双方签署。
words.en: Something that is legitimate is acceptable according to the law.

words.tr: v. 使有生气；使活跃；使快活
words.ex: The music enlivened the party.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让派对更热闹了。
words.en: To make something more interesting, exciting, or cheerful.

words.tr:
v. （使）磨损；（使）烦躁；（使）紧张
n. 磨损处；吵闹；争吵
words.ex: The rope began to fray after years of use.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子用了多年后开始磨损。
words.en: If something such as cloth or rope frays, or if something frays it, its threads or fibres start to come apart from each other and it becomes weaker. A situation of conflict or intense competition can also be referred to as a fray.

words.ex: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班同学面前让自己丢脸了。
words.en: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel shy, ashamed, or guilty about something.

words.tr: v. 充分满足，使饱享； 使厌腻
words.ex: The rich food sated her hunger.
words.ex_cn: 丰盛的食物满足了她的饥饿感。
words.en: To satisfy a desire or an appetite to the full.

words.tr:
n. 跛子；（身体部分或全部肢体）有缺陷的人
v. 使成瘸子；严重损坏（削弱）
words.ex: The cripple walked slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 那个跛子拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: If someone is crippled by an injury, it is so serious that they can never move their body properly again. A cripple is a person who is severely disabled or unable to walk because of damage to their body.

words.ex: The system will validate your password.
words.ex_cn: 系统将验证你的密码。
words.en: To validate something such as a claim or statement means to prove or confirm that it is true or correct.

words.ex: The wind unbalanced the cyclist.
words.ex_cn: 风让骑自行车的人失去平衡。
words.en: To cause to lose balance or stability; to disturb the equilibrium of.

words.tr: v. 使麻痹；使瘫痪；使无效；使停止活动
words.ex: The accident paralyzed his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿瘫痪了。
words.en: If someone is paralyzed by an accident or an illness, they have no feeling in their body, or in part of their body, and are unable to move.

words.ex: Your body metabolize food to get energy.
words.ex_cn: 你的身体通过新陈代谢食物来获取能量。
words.en: To metabolize means to process a substance in the body by metabolism.

words.tr: v. 使预先有倾向；使易接受；使易于患（病）
words.ex: Genes can predispose a person to diabetes.
words.ex_cn: 基因可能使人更容易患糖尿病。
words.en: If something predisposes you to think or behave in a particular way, it makes it likely that you will think or behave in that way.

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.ex: He played a prerecorded message to the audience.
words.ex_cn: 他向观众播放了一段预先录制的音频。
words.en: To record something in advance, especially a radio or television program.

words.ex: He abbreviates the word 'example' as 'ex.'.
words.ex_cn: 他把单词 'example' 缩写为 'ex.'。
words.en: To abbreviate something means to make it shorter, especially by using a particular word or phrase to represent it.

words.ex: The nail protrudes from the wood.
words.ex_cn: 钉子从木头里凸出来。
words.en: If something protrudes from somewhere, it sticks out.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.tr: v. 使气馁；使胆怯；吓倒
words.ex: The loud noise did not daunt her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音并没有吓倒她。
words.en: If something daunts you, it makes you feel slightly afraid or worried about dealing with it.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.tr:
v. 稀释
adj. 经稀释的
words.ex: He dilutes the juice with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水稀释果汁。
words.en: To dilute a liquid means to make it thinner or weaker by adding water or another liquid to it.

words.tr: v. 熄灭；平息；抑制（欲望）；用水冷却
words.ex: He quenched the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水熄灭了火。
words.en: To satisfy one's thirst or to extinguish a fire or to suppress a feeling or desire.

words.ex: She will sterilize the bottles before use.
words.ex_cn: 她将在使用前消毒瓶子。
words.en: To sterilize something means to make it completely clean and free from bacteria.

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.ex: The doctor advised him to drink more water to help him urinate more frequently.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议他多喝水，以帮助他更频繁地排尿。
words.en: To urinate means to pass urine from the body.

words.tr: v. 使可见；使形象化；设想；
words.ex: He uses maps to visualize the data.
words.ex_cn: 他使用地图来使数据可见。
words.en: If you visualize something, you imagine what it is like by forming a mental picture of it.

words.ex: The sun wakens the birds every morning.
words.ex_cn: 太阳每天早晨唤醒鸟儿。
words.en: to stop sleeping or to make someone stop sleeping

words.tr:
v. 虚张声势；唬人
n. 虚张声势；吓唬；峭壁
adj. 直率的
words.ex: He used a bluff to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚张声势赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you bluff, you try to make someone believe that you will do something when you do not really intend to do it, or that you know something when you do not really know it.

words.tr: v. 叙述；给（电视或电影）作旁白
words.ex: He will narrate the story to his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他将为他的小妹妹讲述这个故事。
words.en: If you narrate a story, you tell it from your own point of view.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.ex: He alleges that the manager stole money.
words.ex_cn: 他声称经理偷了钱。
words.en: If you allege that something bad is true, you say it but do not prove it.

words.tr: v. 淹没；泛滥；使不胜负荷；使应接不暇
words.ex: The rain inundated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 大雨淹没了这个小镇。
words.en: To inundate means to flood or overwhelm something with a large amount of water or things.

words.ex: He wants to emigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.tr: v. 用言语（或文字）表达
words.ex: He can verbalize his thoughts clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: To verbalize means to express something in words, especially to articulate feelings or thoughts clearly.

words.ex: He did not avail himself of the opportunity.
words.ex_cn: 他没有利用这个机会。
words.en: If you avail yourself of something, you use it or take advantage of it.

words.ex: The plastic is preformed before being molded into the final product.
words.ex_cn: 塑料在成型为最终产品之前先进行预成型。
words.en: To shape or form something in advance, especially before it is used in a final product or process.

words.tr: v. 改变（说法、决定等）；原路返回；倒回
words.ex: The algorithm backtracks when it encounters a dead end.
words.ex_cn: 该算法在遇到死胡同时会回溯。
words.en: To go back over the course by which one has come.

words.ex: The sun reappeared after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，太阳重新出现了。
words.en: If someone or something reappears, they appear again after they have been away or out of sight for some time.

words.ex: He will subdivide the land into two parts.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地分成两部分。
words.en: If something is subdivided, it is divided into several smaller areas, parts, or sections.

words.ex: The heat is reradiated from the surface of the object.
words.ex_cn: 热量从物体表面再辐射出来。
words.en: To radiate again or anew; to emit energy, especially heat or light, after absorbing it from another source.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr:
n. 曲柄杖；钩；弯曲处；骗子
v. （使）弯曲；使成钩状
words.ex: The old man walked with a wooden crook.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人拿着一根木制曲柄杖走路。
words.en: A crook is a person who is dishonest or a criminal, or it can refer to a bend or curve in something.

words.ex: The child outgrew his shoes in one year.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子一年内就长高了，鞋子都穿不下了。
words.en: If you outgrow a particular way of behaving or thinking, you change and become more mature, so that you no longer behave or think in that way.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: He used a stick to fend off the dog.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子挡开了那只狗。
words.en: To fend means to defend or protect oneself from something, or to manage to survive or cope without help.

words.ex: The king tried to subjugate the rebels.
words.ex_cn: 国王试图征服叛乱者。
words.en: To subjugate a country or group of people means to take complete control of them, especially by defeating them in a war.

words.tr: v. 课税过重；负担过度；使工作过度
words.ex: The high taxes overtax the poor families.
words.ex_cn: 高额税收压垮了贫困家庭。
words.en: To impose too much tax on someone or something, or to make excessive demands on someone's strength or resources.

words.tr: v. 用喙整理羽毛；精心打扮；感觉良好
words.ex: The bird preens its feathers every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟每天早上梳理它的羽毛。
words.en: If a bird preens or preens itself, it cleans and arranges its feathers using its beak.

words.ex: The judge will uphold the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官将维护法律。
words.en: If you uphold something such as a law, a principle, or a decision, you support and maintain it.

words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.ex: The horror movie showed a man being dismembered.
words.ex_cn: 那部恐怖电影展示了一名男子被肢解。
words.en: To dismember means to cut, tear, or pull the limbs from a body.

words.ex: The wound will heal in a few days.
words.ex_cn: 伤口几天后就会愈合。
words.en: To make or become healthy or whole again; to cure or recover from an injury or illness.

words.tr: v. 使中立；中和；使无效
words.ex: The government tried to neutralize the conflict by talking to both sides.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图通过与双方交谈来使冲突中立化。
words.en: To neutralize something means to stop it from having any effect or to make it ineffective.

words.tr: v. 重新排列；重新安排
words.ex: He rearranged the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他把书架上的书重新排列了。
words.en: If you rearrange the objects in a place, you change the way in which they are organized or positioned.

words.ex: After the war, many families had to resettle in new countries.
words.ex_cn: 战争结束后，许多家庭不得不在新国家重新定居。
words.en: To settle or cause to settle in a different place.

words.ex: We can redefine the rules to make the game more fun.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以重新定义规则，让游戏更有趣。
words.en: To define something again or differently, especially in order to give it a new or improved meaning.

words.ex: He rediscovered his love for music after years.
words.ex_cn: 多年后，他重新发现了对音乐的热爱。
words.en: To discover again something that was lost or forgotten.

words.ex: He regained his strength after rest.
words.ex_cn: 他休息后恢复了体力。
words.en: If you regain something that you have lost, you get it back again.

words.tr:
v. 重新进入
n. 重进入
words.ex: After a brief break, she reentered the room.
words.ex_cn: 短暂的休息后，她再次进入了房间。
words.en: To enter again.

words.tr: v. 重新露面；重铺路面
words.ex: He resurfaced after being missing for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 他在失踪数周后重新露面。
words.en: If someone or something resurfaces, they appear again after being unseen or unheard of for a period of time.

words.ex: The argument started small but soon escalate.
words.ex_cn: 争论起初很小，但很快逐步升高。
words.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.ex: One apple will suffice for now.
words.ex_cn: 一个苹果现在就足够了。
words.en: If something suffices, it is enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfill a need.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.tr: adj. 不合时宜的；过早发生的
words.ex: His untimely death shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他突如其来的去世让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: If you describe an event as untimely, you mean that it happened earlier than it should, or sooner than you expected.

words.tr:
adv. 彻底地；立刻地；
adj. 完全的；彻底的；
words.ex: He refused the offer outright.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: If something is done outright, it is done completely and without any hesitation or attempt to hide it.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；安详的
words.ex: The lake is serene in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的湖面很宁静。
words.en: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled; tranquil.

words.ex: His room is messy with clothes everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 他的房间很杂乱，衣服到处都是。
words.en: If you describe something as messy, you mean that it is untidy or dirty.

words.ex: The scruffy dog wandered around the alley.
words.ex_cn: 那只邋遢的狗在小巷里游荡。
words.en: If someone or something is scruffy, they are untidy and look a little dirty.

words.tr: adj. 包容的；包含全部费用的；
words.ex: The school is inclusive and welcomes all students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校是包容的，欢迎所有学生。
words.en: Inclusive is used to describe something that is designed to include all types of people, things, or ideas, and to treat them all fairly and equally.

words.tr: adj. 暴虐的；压制的；残暴的
words.ex: The tyrannical king punished people for small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 这个暴虐的国王因为小错误惩罚人民。
words.en: Using power in a cruel and unfair way over people in a country or group.

words.tr: adj. 悲伤的；使人伤心的
words.ex: He looked sorrowful after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 失去狗后，他看起来很悲伤。
words.en: Feeling or showing sadness; mournful.

words.ex: The dorsal fin helps the fish swim steadily.
words.ex_cn: 背鳍帮助鱼稳定游动。
words.en: Relating to the back or posterior part of an organism or structure.

words.ex: The windblown leaves covered the ground.
words.ex_cn: 被风吹落的叶子覆盖了地面。
words.en: Carried or shaped by the wind.

words.tr: adj. 受大风吹的；风刮的
words.ex: The windswept hill had no trees.
words.ex_cn: 风刮过的山丘上没有树。
words.en: Exposed to or swept by the wind.

words.tr: v. 再执行；“reexecute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The program was reexecuted to ensure the accuracy of the results.
words.ex_cn: 程序被重新执行以确保结果的准确性。
words.en: To execute something again, especially after changes have been made.

words.ex: There was a torrential rain last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚下了一场猛烈的雨。
words.en: Used to describe something that is like a torrent; very heavy or fast and powerful.

words.ex: He is clumsy and dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他很笨拙，把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: A clumsy person moves or handles things in a careless, awkward way, often so that things are knocked over or broken.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.ex: The cost is proportional to the size.
words.ex_cn: 成本与大小成比例。
words.en: If one amount is proportional to another, the two amounts increase and decrease at the same rate so there is always the same relationship between them.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.ex: Reptiles are poikilothermic animals that rely on external heat sources.
words.ex_cn: 爬行动物是依赖外部热源的冷血动物。
words.en: Poikilothermic refers to organisms that cannot regulate their body temperature, so it varies with the temperature of their surroundings.

words.ex: The normative approach to ethics focuses on what should be done.
words.ex_cn: 规范伦理学的方法侧重于应该做什么。
words.en: Normative means relating to an ideal standard or model, or being based on what is considered to be the usual or correct way of doing something.

words.ex: The landscape was flattish with only a few gentle hills.
words.ex_cn: 这片风景稍显平坦，只有几座缓坡的小山。
words.en: Somewhat flat; having a surface that is not completely flat but is nearly so.

words.ex: She wore a chic dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条别致的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as chic, you mean that they are stylish and fashionable.

words.tr: adj. 温文儒雅的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: He is an urbane man who speaks politely.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个举止文雅、说话有礼貌的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as urbane, you mean that they are polite, confident, and comfortable in social situations.

words.ex: The subglacial lake was discovered using advanced radar technology.
words.ex_cn: 这个冰川下的湖泊是使用先进的雷达技术发现的。
words.en: Located or occurring beneath a glacier or ice sheet.

words.ex: The wavy line looks like a snake.
words.ex_cn: 波浪形的线看起来像一条蛇。
words.en: Something that is wavy has a series of curves or waves in it.

words.ex: The sea was choppy, making it difficult to sail.
words.ex_cn: 海面波涛汹涌，使得航行变得困难。
words.en: If the sea or a river is choppy, the water moves in a lot of small waves because it is windy or because the current is strong.

words.tr: adj. 增补性的；补充性的；
words.ex: The teacher gave supplementary notes for the lesson.
words.ex_cn: 老师为这节课提供了增补性的笔记。
words.en: Supplementary things are added to something in order to improve it or make it more complete.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；无保障的；缺乏自信的；无把握的
words.ex: He feels insecure when he is alone at night.
words.ex_cn: 当他晚上一个人时，他感到不安全。
words.en: If you are insecure, you lack confidence because you think that you are not good enough or are not loved.

words.tr: adj. 不被注意的；被忽视的；
words.ex: The unnoticed crack in the wall grew bigger.
words.ex_cn: 墙上的那条不被注意的裂缝变大了。
words.en: If something happens or passes unnoticed, it is not seen or observed by anyone.

words.tr: adj. 无形状的；样子不好看的
words.ex: The dress hung shapelessly on her thin frame.
words.ex_cn: 那件衣服松松垮垮地挂在她瘦削的身体上。
words.en: If something is described as shapeless, it does not have a distinct or attractive shape.

words.ex: He is dishonest when he lies about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 当他谎报作业时，他是不诚实的。
words.en: If you say that someone is dishonest, you mean that they are not honest and you cannot trust them.

words.ex: The ghost is nonexistent.
words.ex_cn: 这个幽灵是不存在的。
words.en: If you say that something is nonexistent, you mean that it does not exist when you feel that it should.

words.ex: It is improbable that he will arrive on time.
words.ex_cn: 他准时到达的可能性很小。
words.en: If you describe something as improbable, you mean it is unlikely to be true or to happen.

words.ex: The rain was unending.
words.ex_cn: 雨下个不停。
words.en: Something that is unending seems to have no end or to last forever.

words.ex: He was known for his uncorrupt and honest dealings.
words.ex_cn: 他以不腐败和诚实的交易而闻名。
words.en: Not corrupt; free from corruption or bribery.

words.ex: It is unreasonable to expect help without asking.
words.ex_cn: 不请求帮助就指望别人帮忙是不合理的。
words.en: If you say that someone is being unreasonable, you mean that they are behaving in a way that is not fair or sensible.

words.tr: adj. 不愿合作的；不愿配合的
words.ex: He was uncooperative during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试中不配合。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncooperative, you mean that they do not want to help or support other people.

words.ex: She remained unexcited even in the face of danger.
words.ex_cn: 即使面对危险，她依然保持镇定。
words.en: If you are unexcited about something, you are not enthusiastic or eager about it.

words.tr: adj. 无结果的；无成效的；
words.ex: The meeting was fruitless because no decisions were made.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议毫无结果，因为没有做出任何决定。
words.en: If an action or attempt to do something is fruitless, it is unsuccessful or produces nothing of value.

words.ex: The field remained unseeded after the drought.
words.ex_cn: 干旱过后，田地仍然未播种。
words.en: Not having been seeded; especially in sports, not having been designated as a seed in a tournament.

words.tr: adj. 不确切的；不精确的；
words.ex: His answer was imprecise and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不确切，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as imprecise, you mean that it is not stated or done accurately or clearly.

words.tr: adj. 不可否认的；无可辩驳的
words.ex: The evidence is undeniable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是不可否认的。
words.en: If you say that something is undeniable, you mean that it is definitely true or that it definitely exists.

words.ex: The effects of this change are unobservable to the human eye.
words.ex_cn: 这种变化的效果是人眼难以察觉的。
words.en: If something is unobservable, it cannot be observed or detected by any means.

words.tr: adj. 难识别的；觉察不出的
words.ex: The distant mountains were indiscernible in the fog.
words.ex_cn: 远处的山在雾中难以辨认。
words.en: If something is indiscernible, it is impossible to see or understand clearly.

words.tr: adj. 难以置信的；不可想象的；
words.ex: The damage from the storm was unimaginable.
words.ex_cn: 风暴造成的破坏难以置信。
words.en: If you describe something as unimaginable, you are emphasizing that it is difficult to imagine or understand because it is not part of people's normal experience.

words.ex: The rules are inflexible and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则是不灵活的，不能更改。
words.en: If you say that someone is inflexible, you are criticizing them because they refuse to change their mind or alter their way of doing things.

words.ex: The boat has a watertight hull.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船有一个不透水的船体。
words.en: Something that is watertight does not allow water to pass through it, often used to describe containers, compartments, or arguments that are completely secure and cannot be faulted.

words.tr: adj. 不明智的；轻率的；欠考虑的
words.ex: It is unwise to walk alone at night.
words.ex_cn: 晚上独自走路是不明智的。
words.en: If you describe something as unwise, you mean that it is foolish and likely to lead to a bad result.

words.ex: The thick forest was impenetrable.
words.ex_cn: 这片茂密的森林无法穿越。
words.en: Impenetrable is used to describe something that cannot be passed through, entered, or understood.

words.ex: The remote village is unreachable by road during the rainy season.
words.ex_cn: 这个偏远村庄在雨季期间无法通过道路到达。
words.en: If you describe something as unreachable, you mean that it cannot be reached, accessed, or achieved.

words.ex: He is intolerant of people who are late.
words.ex_cn: 他不能容忍迟到的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as intolerant, you mean that they do not accept behavior and opinions that are different from their own.

words.tr: adj. 不能渗透的；不受影响的
words.ex: The coat is impervious to rain.
words.ex_cn: 这件外套不透水。
words.en: If you are impervious to someone's actions, you are not affected or influenced by them.

words.tr: adj. 不能架桥的；不可逾越的；无法弥合的
words.ex: The gap between them was unbridgeable.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的鸿沟是无法跨越的。
words.en: If a gap or difference is unbridgeable, it is so large or so great that it cannot be bridged or made any smaller.

words.tr: adj. 倾向一方的；不平衡的；悬殊的
words.ex: The game was lopsided, and one team won by 10 points.
words.ex_cn: 这场比赛比分悬殊，一支队伍以10分获胜。
words.en: Something that is lopsided is uneven because one side is lower or heavier than the other.

words.ex: Some bird species are nonmigratory and stay in the same region all year round.
words.ex_cn: 一些鸟类是不迁移的，全年都停留在同一地区。
words.en: Not migrating; remaining in the same area throughout the year.

words.ex: He reluctantly agreed to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不情愿地同意帮助他的朋友。
words.en: If you do something reluctantly, you do it unwillingly.

words.tr: adj. 不兼容的；不相配的；
words.ex: The software is incompatible with old systems.
words.ex_cn: 这个软件与旧系统不兼容。
words.en: If one thing or person is incompatible with another, they are very different in important ways, and do not suit each other or agree with each other.

words.tr: adj. 不警觉的；粗心大意的；不提防的
words.ex: He was unwary and lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他没有警惕，丢了钱包。
words.en: If you describe someone as unwary, you mean that they are not cautious or experienced and are therefore likely to be harmed or deceived.

words.ex: This glass is unbreakable.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃不易破损。
words.en: If something is unbreakable, it cannot be broken or damaged.

words.ex: The difference in their heights was unnoticeable.
words.ex_cn: 他们身高的差异不明显。
words.en: If something is unnoticeable, it is not easily seen or noticed.

words.ex: He has an insatiable hunger for knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识有着无法满足的渴望。
words.en: If someone is insatiable, they always want more of something and are never satisfied.

words.tr: adj. 不敬的；不逊的；无礼的
words.ex: He made an irreverent joke about the king.
words.ex_cn: 他对国王开了一个不敬的玩笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as irreverent, you mean that they do not show respect for people or things that are generally respected.

words.ex: The museum houses a collection of relict artifacts from ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆收藏了古代文明的残余文物。
words.en: A relict is something which has survived from an earlier period of time, especially when it is the only remaining example of its kind.

words.ex: The cruel king punished the innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 残酷的国王惩罚了无辜的人。
words.en: Someone who is cruel deliberately causes pain or distress to others or feels no concern about it.

words.tr: adj. 残忍的；无情的；无慈悲心的；
words.ex: The merciless storm destroyed the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场残忍的风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: If you describe someone as merciless, you mean that they are very cruel or determined and do not show any concern for the effect their actions have on other people.

words.ex: The storm caused a brutal flood that destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了残酷的洪水，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.

words.ex: The operational system runs smoothly every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个运作系统每天运行顺畅。
words.en: If a system or service is operational, it is working or able to be used.

words.tr: adj. 仓促马虎的；毛躁的；潦草的
words.ex: He gave a slapdash answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个草率的回答。
words.en: If you say that something is done in a slapdash way, you mean that it is done carelessly and quickly, without much attention to detail.

words.ex: The rock layers were interbedded with layers of shale.
words.ex_cn: 岩石层与页岩层交错。
words.en: Lying between layers of a different kind of rock or sediment.

words.tr: adj. 泛滥的；猖獗的；蔓生的
words.ex: Rumors are rampant in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 谣言在这个小镇上四处流传。
words.en: If you describe something bad, such as a crime or disease, as rampant, you mean that it is very common and is increasing in an uncontrolled way.

words.ex: He gave a derisive laugh when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时，他发出了一声嘲笑的笑。
words.en: expressing contempt or ridicule.

words.tr: adj. 不快乐的；忧郁的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room was cheerless and dark.
words.ex_cn: 房间阴暗而无生气。
words.en: If you describe a place or a thing as cheerless, you mean that it is dull and depressing.

words.ex: He was hesitant to answer the question.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着不敢回答这个问题。
words.en: If you are hesitant about doing something, you are slow to do it, usually because you are uncertain, worried, or nervous about it.

words.ex: He has a sweaty forehead after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后额头满是汗。
words.en: If something is sweaty, it is covered in sweat or causes sweat.

words.ex: The leaky roof lets rain in during storms.
words.ex_cn: 这个漏雨的屋顶在暴风雨时会让雨水进来。
words.en: Allowing liquid or gas to pass through a hole or crack.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.tr: adj. 处女（般）的；贞洁的；纯真的
words.ex: She had a virginal complexion that seemed untouched by the world.
words.ex_cn: 她有着一种似乎未被世俗触碰过的无瑕肤色。
words.en: A virginal thing is pure, untouched, or in its original condition, especially in the context of something that has not been used or developed.

words.ex: He ran so fast that he became breathless.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得太快，结果气喘吁吁。
words.en: If you are breathless, you have difficulty in breathing properly, for example because you have been running or because you are afraid or excited.

words.ex: He was a onetime teacher before becoming a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他在成为作家之前是一名教师。
words.en: Former or previous in time; having existed or occurred at an earlier time.

words.tr: adj. 雷声隆隆的；雷鸣般的
words.ex: The audience gave a thunderous applause.
words.ex_cn: 观众们报以雷鸣般的掌声。
words.en: If you describe a noise as thunderous, you mean that it is very loud and deep.

words.ex: The cerebral cortex controls thinking and memory.
words.ex_cn: 大脑皮层控制思考和记忆。
words.en: Relating to the brain or the intellect.

words.ex: The painting is representational and shows a clear tree.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是具象的，画了一棵清晰的树。
words.en: Representational art or painting shows things as they actually appear in real life.

words.tr: adj. 单色的； 单频的（光、辐射等）
words.ex: The painting is monochromatic, using only shades of blue.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是单色的，只使用了不同深浅的蓝色。
words.en: Consisting of one color or wavelength.

words.ex: The timid boy whispered his answer.
words.ex_cn: 这个害羞的男孩小声说出了他的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or actions as timid, you are criticizing them for being too cautious or slow to act, because they are nervous about the possible consequences of their actions.

words.ex: The triangle has three equal sides and is equilateral.
words.ex_cn: 这个三角形有三条相等的边，是等边的。
words.en: Having all sides or faces equal.

words.ex: The temperature dropped to subfreezing levels during the night.
words.ex_cn: 夜间气温降至冰点以下。
words.en: Below the freezing point of water.

words.ex: He gave an antagonistic reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了敌对的答复。
words.en: If someone is antagonistic to someone or something, they show hatred or opposition towards them.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.ex: The geopolitical situation in the region is complex.
words.ex_cn: 该地区的地缘政治局势复杂。
words.en: Relating to the study of the effects of geography (human and physical) on international politics and international relations.

words.ex: The rock shows geochemical changes over time.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石随着时间显示出地球化学变化。
words.en: Relating to the chemistry of the earth and its rocks and minerals.

words.tr: adj. 地球外的；地外的；外星球的；
words.ex: The movie shows an extraterrestrial life form.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一种地球外的生命形式。
words.en: An extraterrestrial is a creature that comes from or exists outside the planet Earth.

words.ex: The scientists study geophysical patterns in the earth.
words.ex_cn: 科学家们研究地球的地球物理模式。
words.en: Relating to the branch of science concerned with the physical processes and phenomena occurring in the earth and its atmosphere.

words.tr: adj. 图上没标明的；无人涉足的；未知的
words.ex: The explorers sailed into uncharted waters.
words.ex_cn: 探险家们驶入了未被探索的水域。
words.en: If you describe a situation, experience, or activity as uncharted, you mean that it is new and unfamiliar, and therefore difficult to predict or understand.

words.ex: The event was highly televisual, capturing the attention of millions.
words.ex_cn: 这一事件非常适合上电视镜头，吸引了数百万人的注意。
words.en: Relating to or suitable for television.

words.tr: adj. 向东的；从东方来的
words.ex: The ship sailed in an easterly direction.
words.ex_cn: 船向东航行。
words.en: An easterly point, area, or direction is to the east or towards the east.

words.ex: The stagnant pond emitted a miasmic odor.
words.ex_cn: 死水潭散发出有害的气味。
words.en: Relating to or resembling a noxious atmosphere or influence.

words.ex: The city is known for its multistoried buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市以其多层建筑而闻名。
words.en: Having several stories or layers.

words.ex: The multistory building has ten floors.
words.ex_cn: 这座多层建筑有十层。
words.en: Having several or many stories or floors.

words.ex: He bought a secondhand bike for $50.
words.ex_cn: 他花50美元买了一辆二手自行车。
words.en: Something that is secondhand is not new and has been owned by someone else before.

words.ex: The luminous moon lights up the night.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的月亮照亮了夜晚。
words.en: Something that is luminous shines or glows in the dark.

words.ex: The children were running in a frenetic way around the room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房间里发狂似的跑来跑去。
words.en: If you describe an activity as frenetic, you mean that it is fast and energetic, but rather uncontrolled and often not very well organized.

words.ex: The bread had turned mouldy in the damp environment.
words.ex_cn: 面包在潮湿的环境中已经发霉了。
words.en: Something that is mouldy is covered with mould.

words.tr: adj. 温和宜人的（气候）；芳香的
words.ex: The balmy wind felt nice on her skin.
words.ex_cn: 温暖的微风轻拂她的皮肤。
words.en: Balmy weather is pleasantly warm and mild.

words.tr: adj. 非本质的；不重要的
words.ex: The ornament is nonessential to the room.
words.ex_cn: 这个装饰品对房间来说是非必需的。
words.en: Something that is nonessential is not absolutely necessary.

words.tr: adj. 不合常规的；不符合惯例的；不寻常的；
words.ex: He wears unconventional clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿不合常规的衣服来引人注目。
words.en: If you describe a person or their attitude or behaviour as unconventional, you mean that they do not behave in the same way as most other people in their society.

words.ex: He wears untraditional clothes to school.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着不传统的衣服去学校。
words.en: Not based on or conforming to what is generally done or believed.

words.ex: He prefers using nonelectronic typewriters for their tactile feel.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢使用非电子打字机，因为它们有触感。
words.en: Not involving or using electronic devices or technology.

words.ex: The regime was criticized for its nondemocratic practices.
words.ex_cn: 该政权因其非民主的做法而受到批评。
words.en: Not democratic; not characterized by or supporting democracy.

words.ex: The nonfarm payroll data is a key economic indicator.
words.ex_cn: 非农就业数据是一个关键的经济指标。
words.en: Relating to economic activities or sectors that are not involved in agriculture.

words.ex: The store sells a variety of nonfood items.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种非食物商品。
words.en: Nonfood items are products that are not intended for consumption as food, such as cleaning supplies, home decor, and personal care items.

words.ex: His unselective reading habits led to a broad but shallow knowledge base.
words.ex_cn: 他不加选择地阅读习惯导致知识广博但浅显。
words.en: Not selective; not making or based on careful selection.

words.tr: adj. 诽谤的；损害名誉的
words.ex: The article was filled with libelous accusations.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章充满了诽谤性的指控。
words.en: If a statement in a book, newspaper, or magazine is libelous, it falsely harms the reputation of a person or organization.

words.ex: The phenomenon was unexplainable by current scientific theories.
words.ex_cn: 这种现象用当前的科学理论无法解释。
words.en: If something is unexplainable, there is no possible explanation for it.

words.ex: The flowers are aromatic and fill the garden with scent.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是芳香的，使花园充满香气。
words.en: Having a pleasant and distinctive smell.

words.ex: Hiking up the mountain was a strenuous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰苦的任务。
words.en: Requiring or using great effort or exertion.

words.ex: The obedient child cleaned his room without being told.
words.ex_cn: 这个听话的孩子没被要求就打扫了房间。
words.en: An obedient person or animal does what they are told to do.

words.ex: The big company owns a subsidiary that makes phones.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司拥有一家生产手机的附属公司。
words.en: A subsidiary is a company which is part of a larger and more important company.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；起破坏作用的
n. 腐蚀性物品
words.ex: The acid is corrosive and can damage metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸具有腐蚀性，会损坏金属。
words.en: A corrosive substance is able to destroy solid materials by a chemical reaction.

words.tr: adj. 有深刻了解的；富有洞察力的
words.ex: His insightful comment helped us understand the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他富有洞察力的评论帮助我们理解了这个问题。
words.en: If you describe someone or their remarks as insightful, you mean that they show a very good understanding of people and situations.

words.tr: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的；
words.ex: She wore a glamorous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条富有魅力的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as glamorous, you mean that they are more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

words.ex: I am grateful for your help.
words.ex_cn: 我感激你的帮助。
words.en: If you are grateful for something that someone has given you or done for you, you have warm, friendly feelings towards them and wish to thank them.

words.tr: adj. 使感动的；感情的；动感情的
words.ex: The movie used emotive music to make people cry.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影用了富有情感的音乐来让人流泪。
words.en: If you describe something as emotive, you mean that it is concerned with emotions and feelings, and often causes them.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.tr: adj. 高傲的；贵族气派的
words.ex: He carried himself with a lordly air.
words.ex_cn: 他带着一种高傲的气派。
words.en: If you say that someone is lordly, you are critical of them because they behave in a proud and arrogant way, as if they are better than other people.

words.ex: They eat at an upscale restaurant every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周末都在一家高档餐厅吃饭。
words.en: If you describe something as upscale, you mean it is of high quality or intended for people who are wealthy.

words.tr:
adv. 进一步；更远；此外；
adj. 更多的；附加的；
v. 促进；
words.ex: He explained the problem, and then gave further examples.
words.ex_cn: 他解释了这个问题，然后给出了进一步的例子。
words.en: to a greater degree or extent

words.ex: The hospital is an institutional building.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一座大型机构的建筑。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of an institution, especially a large organization or public body.

words.ex: The judge made an equitable decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个公平的决定。
words.en: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally.

words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.ex: He was deferential to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师很恭敬。
words.en: If you are deferential, you are polite and respectful towards someone, especially because they have a higher position or status than you.

words.ex: His lazy habits were contributory to his failure.
words.ex_cn: 他懒惰的习惯促成了他的失败。
words.en: Playing a part in bringing about a result or helping something to advance.

words.ex: The plan was ill-conceived and failed quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划构思不当，很快就失败了。
words.en: If you describe a plan, idea, or action as ill-conceived, you mean that it is likely to fail or cause problems because it has not been thought about carefully enough.

words.ex: Paleomagnetic studies help us understand ancient geomagnetic fields.
words.ex_cn: 古地磁研究帮助我们理解古代地磁场。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the branch of geophysics concerned with the study of the Earth's magnetic field in the geological past.

words.ex: The museum's paleontological exhibits are fascinating for both children and adults.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆的古生物学展品对成人和儿童都非常有吸引力。
words.en: Relating to the branch of science concerned with fossil animals and plants.

words.tr: adj. 灌木的；灌木状的；灌木丛生的
words.ex: The hillside was covered in shrubby vegetation.
words.ex_cn: 山坡上覆盖着灌木丛生的植被。
words.en: Consisting of or resembling shrubs.

words.ex: The glorious sunset lit up the whole sky.
words.ex_cn: 辉煌的日落染红了整个天空。
words.en: Something that is glorious is very beautiful and impressive.

words.tr:
adj. 辐射状的；放射式的；径向的；星形的
n. 子午线轮胎；辐射式轮胎
words.ex: The wheels have radial tires.
words.ex_cn: 这些车轮装有径向轮胎。
words.en: Relating to or situated near the radius or the radial side of the forearm or hand.

words.tr: adj. 偷偷摸摸的；不声张的；秘密的
words.ex: The thief moved with stealthy steps.
words.ex_cn: 小偷蹑手蹑脚地移动。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as stealthy, you mean that they are quiet and secret in what they do, often because they do not want to be seen or heard.

words.ex: The meeting was fruitful and solved many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议富有成效，解决了许多问题。
words.en: Producing good or helpful results; productive.

words.ex: He faced undue pressure from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他受到了来自老板的过度压力。
words.en: If you describe something bad as undue, you mean that it is greater or more extreme than you think is reasonable or appropriate.

words.ex: His answer was too simplistic.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答太简单化了。
words.en: If you describe something as simplistic, you disapprove of it because it is so simple that it ignores important details or difficulties.

words.ex: The undersea cable connects two countries.
words.ex_cn: 这条海底电缆连接了两个国家。
words.en: Located, occurring, or used beneath the surface of the sea.

words.ex: The expedition focused on oceanographic research.
words.ex_cn: 这次探险专注于海洋学研究。
words.en: Relating to the branch of science that deals with the physical and biological properties and phenomena of the sea.

words.ex: The soil was too limy for the plants to grow well.
words.ex_cn: 土壤含石灰过多，植物无法良好生长。
words.en: Containing or resembling lime.

words.tr: adj. 纤维构成的；纤维状的；
words.ex: The banana peel is fibrous and hard to digest.
words.ex_cn: 香蕉皮是纤维构成的，难以消化。
words.en: Something that is fibrous contains fibres or is made up of fibres.

words.ex: The silvery moon lit up the lake.
words.ex_cn: 银色的月光照亮了湖面。
words.en: Something that is silvery looks like silver or is the color of silver.

words.tr: adj. 无望的；凄凉的；荒凉的；
words.ex: The future looks bleak without a job.
words.ex_cn: 没有工作，未来看起来毫无希望。
words.en: If you describe a situation as bleak, you mean that it seems unlikely to improve or get better.

words.ex: Xerophytic plants are adapted to survive in dry environments.
words.ex_cn: 旱生植物适应在干燥环境中生存。
words.en: A xerophytic plant is one that is adapted to survive in an environment with little liquid water, such as a desert or an ice- or snow-covered region in the Alps or the Arctic.

words.ex: This plan is practicable.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的。
words.en: If a task, plan, or idea is practicable, it can be successfully done or achieved.

words.ex: He comes from a seafaring family.
words.ex_cn: 他来自一个航海世家。
words.en: Seafaring relates to travelling by sea, especially as a job or as a way of life.

words.ex: The aero design reduces air resistance.
words.ex_cn: 航空设计减少了空气阻力。
words.en: Relating to aircraft or aeronautics.

words.tr: adj. 无疑问的；确凿的；无可非议的
words.ex: His honesty is unquestionable.
words.ex_cn: 他的诚实是无可置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something as unquestionable, you are emphasizing that it is so obviously true or real that nobody can doubt it.

words.tr: adj. 欢乐的；轻松快活的；好交际的
words.ex: The party was convivial and everyone laughed a lot.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛友好愉快，大家都笑得很开心。
words.en: A convivial atmosphere or event is friendly and pleasant, and people enjoy being together.

words.ex: The clown made a comical face and everyone laughed.
words.ex_cn: 小丑做了一个可笑的表情，大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe something as comical, you mean that it is amusing and makes you laugh.

words.ex: This rule is applicable to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If something is applicable to a particular situation, it is relevant or suitable for that situation.

words.ex: They did a collaborative project in class.
words.ex_cn: 他们在课堂上做了一个合作项目。
words.en: A collaborative piece of work is done by two or more people or groups working together.

words.tr: adj. 横渡大西洋的；大西洋两岸国家的；
words.ex: The transatlantic flight took eight hours.
words.ex_cn: 横渡大西洋的航班花了八个小时。
words.en: Crossing the Atlantic Ocean.

words.tr: adj. 耸人听闻的；极好的；
words.ex: The newspaper published a sensational story about a ghost.
words.ex_cn: 这家报纸刊登了一篇关于幽灵的耸人听闻的消息。
words.en: A sensational event or situation is so remarkable that it causes great excitement and interest.

words.ex: The macroscopic view shows the whole tree.
words.ex_cn: 宏观视角展示了整棵树。
words.en: Large enough to be seen or examined without the use of a microscope.

words.ex: The building has a postmodern design with strange shapes.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑具有后现代主义风格，形状奇特。
words.en: Postmodern is used to describe something that is related to or characteristic of postmodernism, especially in art, literature, or architecture.

words.ex: Some species have a mutualistic relationship, benefiting each other.
words.ex_cn: 一些物种之间存在共生关系，彼此受益。
words.en: Mutualistic refers to a relationship between organisms of different species in which each benefits from the activity of the other.

words.ex: She wore a gorgeous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件华丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you say that something is gorgeous, you mean that it gives you a lot of pleasure or is very attractive.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.ex: He speaks in a conversational tone with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友说话时用会话式的语调。
words.en: Relating to or in the style of a conversation; informal and friendly.

words.tr: adj. 慵懒的；没精打采的；懒洋洋的
words.ex: He felt lethargic after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you are lethargic, you do not have much energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: The frisky puppy was bouncing around the room.
words.ex_cn: 那只活泼的小狗在房间里蹦来蹦去。
words.en: If you describe a person or animal as frisky, you mean they are lively and playful.

words.ex: The Hohokam were known for their advanced irrigation systems.
words.ex_cn: 霍霍坎人以其先进的灌溉系统而闻名。
words.en: A prehistoric Native American culture that existed in the North American Southwest, known for its advanced irrigation systems and architecture.

words.ex: He is an astute businessman who always makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他是个精明的商人，总是做出明智的决定。
words.en: If you describe someone as astute, you think they are clever and can see through things quickly and make good judgments.

words.ex: He showed the utmost care when handling the fragile glass.
words.ex_cn: 他在处理易碎的玻璃时表现出了最大的小心。
words.en: The greatest or highest degree of something.

words.tr: adj. 力大无比的；艰巨的
words.ex: The task ahead is herculean, but we are determined to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 前方的任务艰巨无比，但我们决心要成功。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as herculean, you mean that it is extremely difficult and requires a lot of effort.

words.tr: adj. 记性好的；有保持力的
words.ex: She has a very retentive memory.
words.ex_cn: 她有非常好的记忆力。
words.en: If you have a retentive memory, you are able to remember things easily.

words.tr: adj. 由技术专家组成的
words.ex: The government's technocratic approach to policy-making was criticized for lacking democratic input.
words.ex_cn: 该政府在制定政策时的技术专家治国论方法因缺乏民主参与而受到批评。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by the government or control of society or industry by an elite of technical experts.

words.tr: adj. 像家般舒适的；朴素的；
words.ex: The small cabin had a homely feel with soft blankets and a warm fire.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋有柔软的毛毯和温暖的火炉，感觉像家一样舒适。
words.en: If you describe something as homely, you mean that it is simple and plain, often in a way that is comforting. If you describe a person as homely, you mean that they are not very attractive.

words.tr: adj. （男性）家长制的；族长制的；父权制的
words.ex: He lives in a patriarchal family where the father makes all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他生活在一个父亲做所有决定的父权家庭中。
words.en: Relating to, characteristic of, or denoting a system of society or government controlled by men.

words.ex: The cactus has spiky leaves.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有带尖刺的叶子。
words.en: Something that is spiky has a lot of spikes or sharp points.

words.tr: adj. 更坚实的；更牢固的；更坚固的；“firm”的比较级
words.ex: She needs firmer shoes for hiking.
words.ex_cn: 她徒步旅行需要更结实的鞋子。
words.en: Comparative of firm; more solid, stable, or resolute.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.ex: The roots of the trees were intertwined and intergrown.
words.ex_cn: 这些树的根相互缠绕，连生在一起。
words.en: Grown together or intertwined, especially in a way that makes separation difficult.

words.ex: The composer's latest work is a symphonic masterpiece.
words.ex_cn: 这位作曲家的最新作品是一部交响乐杰作。
words.en: Relating to or having the form or character of a symphony.

words.tr: adj. 更宏伟的；更大的；“grand”的比较级
words.ex: The grander mansion was built in the 19th century.
words.ex_cn: 这座更宏伟的豪宅建于19世纪。
words.en: If you describe something as grander, you mean it is more impressive in size, appearance, or general effect than other things of its kind.

words.tr:
v. 使成锯齿状
adj. 锯齿状的
words.ex: The leaf has a serrate edge.
words.ex_cn: 这片叶子的边缘是锯齿状的。
words.en: Having a notched or toothed edge, especially in reference to the edges of leaves or other plant parts.

words.ex: She has curly hair.
words.ex_cn: 她有一头卷发。
words.en: Having curls or a curved shape.

words.tr:
adj. 抗真菌的
n. 抗真菌药
words.ex: The cream is antifungal and helps heal the rash.
words.ex_cn: 这种药膏具有抗真菌作用，能帮助治愈皮疹。
words.en: Antifungal refers to a substance that is used to treat fungal infections.

words.ex: The accident was avoidable if he had slowed down.
words.ex_cn: 如果他减速了，这场事故本可以避免。
words.en: If something is avoidable, it can be prevented or not done.

words.tr: adj. 可察觉的；可感知的
words.ex: The change is perceivable to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都看得出这个变化。
words.en: Capable of being perceived or noticed; discernible.

words.tr: adj. 可到达的；可访问的；可达成的
words.ex: The island is reachable only by boat.
words.ex_cn: 这个岛屿只能乘船到达。
words.en: If a place or thing is reachable, it is possible to get to it or to achieve it.

words.tr: adj. 可防御的；可保卫的；可辩护的
words.ex: The small castle was defensible with high walls.
words.ex_cn: 这座小城堡有高墙，易于防守。
words.en: Able to be defended or justified.

words.ex: The two parts of the machine are separable for easier transport.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的两部分可以分离，以便于运输。
words.en: Capable of being separated or divided.

words.ex: The accident is attributable to poor road conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这起事故可归因于糟糕的路况。
words.en: Capable of being attributed to someone or something.

words.ex: The teacher believed that every child was educable.
words.ex_cn: 老师相信每个孩子都是可教育的。
words.en: Capable of being educated or trained.

words.tr: adj. 悲惨的；不幸的；难过的；恶劣的
words.ex: He felt wretched after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as wretched, you mean that they are in a very bad or unfortunate situation.

words.ex: The fearsome storm scared everyone.
words.ex_cn: 可怕的风暴吓到了每个人。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as fearsome, you mean that they are frightening, often because they are very large or intense.

words.tr:
adj. 糟糕的；可怕的；
adv. 非常；极其；
words.ex: The weather today is awful.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气很糟糕。
words.en: If you say that something is awful, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, shocking, or bad.

words.ex: The land is highly cultivable and suitable for growing crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片土地非常适合耕种，适宜种植作物。
words.en: Cultivable refers to land that is capable of being cultivated, that is, prepared and used for growing crops.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.tr: adj. 可替换的；可代替的
words.ex: This battery is replaceable.
words.ex_cn: 这个电池是可以更换的。
words.en: If something is replaceable, it can be replaced if it is lost or damaged.

words.ex: The goal is achievable with hard work.
words.ex_cn: 通过努力，这个目标是可以达到的。
words.en: If something is achievable, it is possible to achieve it.

words.ex: Iron is easily oxidizable in the presence of moisture.
words.ex_cn: 铁在潮湿环境中容易氧化。
words.en: Capable of being oxidized.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.tr: adj. 适合刊印的；可印刷的
words.ex: The document is printable and ready for distribution.
words.ex_cn: 该文件可打印并准备分发。
words.en: Capable of being printed or published; suitable for printing.

words.tr: adj. 能用的；耐用的；有用的
words.ex: The old car is still serviceable.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧车仍然可以使用。
words.en: If something is serviceable, it is in good enough condition to be used.

words.ex: This tool is usable for beginners.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具初学者可以用。
words.en: If something is usable, it is in a good enough state or condition to be used.

words.ex: The concept is verbalizable once you understand the underlying principles.
words.ex_cn: 一旦你理解了基本原理，这个概念就可以用言辞表达。
words.en: Capable of being expressed in words.

words.ex: The outcome is foreseeable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是可以预见的。
words.en: If a future event is foreseeable, you know that it will happen or that it can happen, because it is a natural or obvious result of something else that you know.

words.tr: adj. 可运输的；可移动的
words.ex: This box is transportable by truck.
words.ex_cn: 这个箱子可以用卡车运输。
words.en: Capable of being transported or conveyed from one place to another.

words.ex: The chair is designed to be collapsible for easy storage.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子设计成可折叠的，便于存放。
words.en: A collapsible object is designed to be folded into a smaller size for easy storage or transport.

words.ex: The job position is still vacant.
words.ex_cn: 这个职位仍然空缺。
words.en: If something is vacant, it is not being used by anyone.

words.ex: The room is airy with windows on all sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间四面都有窗户，通风很好。
words.en: If a place or room is airy, it has a lot of fresh air because it is large or has a lot of windows.

words.ex: The interstitial spaces in the rock were filled with minerals.
words.ex_cn: 岩石中的空隙被矿物质填满。
words.en: Relating to or situated in the small, narrow spaces between things or parts.

words.ex: The birds flew through the aerial sky.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在空中飞翔。
words.en: An aerial is a wire or rod that sends or receives radio or television signals. As an adjective, aerial describes things that are in the air or related to the air.

words.tr: adj. 有苦味的；激烈而不快的；痛苦的；刺痛的；
words.ex: The medicine tastes bitter.
words.ex_cn: 这种药尝起来很苦。
words.en: Having a sharp, pungent taste or smell; not sweet. Feeling or showing anger, hurt, or resentment because of bad experiences or a sense of unjust treatment.

words.tr: adj. 快的；迅速的；敏捷的；
words.ex: He gave a speedy reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题做出了快速的答复。
words.en: Something that is speedy moves or happens quickly.

words.tr: adj. 充满快乐的；使人高兴的
words.ex: The children were joyous on Christmas morning.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在圣诞节早上非常快乐。
words.en: If you describe something as joyous, you mean that it is full of joy and happiness.

words.ex: He is fanatical about football.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球非常狂热。
words.en: If you describe someone as fanatical, you mean that they are extremely enthusiastic about a particular activity, subject, or belief, often to an extent that is considered excessive or unreasonable.

words.ex: He is slothful and never does his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他懒惰，从不做作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as slothful, you mean that they are lazy.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr: adj. 直言不讳的；直截了当的
words.ex: He was known for his plainspoken manner.
words.ex_cn: 他以说话直率著称。
words.en: If someone is plainspoken, they say exactly what they think, without trying to make their opinions sound more polite or acceptable than they really are.

words.ex: The texture of the dessert was sugarlike, sweet and smooth.
words.ex_cn: 这款甜点的质地糖似的，甜美而顺滑。
words.en: Resembling sugar in taste or appearance.

words.ex: The cumulative score is the total of all previous points.
words.ex_cn: 累积得分是所有之前分数的总和。
words.en: If a series of events have a cumulative effect, each event makes the effect greater.

words.ex: The village has a quaint old church.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄有一座古色古香的古老教堂。
words.en: Something that is quaint is attractive because it is unusual and old-fashioned.

words.ex: The centrifugal force pushes the water outward.
words.ex_cn: 离心力把水向外推。
words.en: Moving or tending to move away from a center.

words.ex: He is an idealistic young man who wants to change the world.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个理想主义的年轻人，想要改变世界。
words.en: If you describe someone as idealistic, you mean that they have ideals, and base their behaviour on these ideals, often in a way that is not practical.

words.tr: adj. 立法的；制定法律的；
words.ex: The legislative branch makes laws.
words.ex_cn: 立法部门制定法律。
words.en: Relating to the making of laws.

words.ex: The box has a cubic shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是立方体形状的。
words.en: Relating to or involving the cube or cubes.

words.ex: The road was paved with bituminous asphalt.
words.ex_cn: 这条路是用沥青混凝土铺成的。
words.en: Containing or resembling bitumen.

words.tr: adj. 有颗粒的；粒状的；有纹的；粗糙的
words.ex: The photograph looked grainy and indistinct.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片看起来颗粒感很强，模糊不清。
